items.title: β-catenin/TCF signaling represses GUCY2C hormone expression through a p38α-GATA2 axis in colorectal cancer
items.blurb: Guanylin (GUCA2A) and uroguanylin (GUCA2B) are paracrine hormone ligands of the tumor-suppressor receptor guanylyl cyclase C (GUCY2C). In early colorectal tumorigenesis, expression of GUCA2A and GUCA2B is silenced through transcriptional repression by APC-regulated {beta}-catenin/TCF signaling, a pathway activated early in malignant transformation. This repression depends on a locus control region (LCR) 1,000-3,683 bp upstream of GUCA2A. Here, we used dCas9-APEX2 biotinylation at genomic elements by restricted spatial tagging (C-BERST) in colorectal cancer (CRC) cell lines with inducible suppression of {beta}-catenin/TCF signaling to identify {beta}-catenin/TCF-regulated proteins associated with the GUCA2A regulatory region that mediate repression of GUCY2C ligand transcription. Guide RNAs were used to direct dCas9-APEX2 for locus-specific proximity biotinylation of proteins. Quantitative mass spectrometry identified p38 (MAPK14) as a candidate regulator enriched near the GUCA2A promoter following {beta}-catenin/TCF suppression. Loss-of-function and rescue experiments established that p38 supports GUCA2A and GUCA2B induction following {beta}-catenin/TCF suppression. Importantly, GATA2 was identified as a p38-dependent activator of GUCA2A and GUCA2B transcription that remained enriched near the GUCA2A promoter independent of {beta}-catenin/TCF signaling. Indeed, GATA2 S192 phosphorylation was reduced by p38 loss and by active {beta}-catenin/TCF signaling. Thus, a p38/GATA2 axis links oncogenic {beta}-catenin/TCF signaling to repression of GUCY2C hormone expression in CRC.

items.title: Ion channel-enhancing nanoparticles reprogram T cells in vivo for cancer immunotherapy
items.blurb: In head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), immunotherapy is frequently ineffective due to the impaired ability of tumor-infiltrating T cells to sustain calcium-dependent cytotoxic effector functions. Kv1.3 potassium channels in T cells are essential for maintaining membrane potential, which is necessary for Ca2+ influx; however, they are suppressed within the tumor microenvironment, and no pharmacologic Kv1.3 activators are currently available. To address this limitation, we developed lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) functionalized with anti-CD5 antibodies to specifically deliver mRNA encoding Kv1.3 (KCNA3) to T cells, thereby increasing channel expression and function. Treatment of human T cells with KCNA3-LNPs resulted in increased Kv1.3 channel protein levels and activity, leading to enhanced Ca2+ influx and elevated secretion of effector cytokines (IL-2, IL-17, TNF-, and IFN-{gamma}) and cytotoxic molecules (Granzyme A, Perforin, Granulysin, and Fas ligand). In a human peripheral blood mononuclear cell-engrafted HNSCC humanized mouse model, peritumoral delivery of KCNA3-LNPs significantly reduced tumor burden and increased the infiltration of CD8 Granzyme B cytotoxic T cells within the tumor, indicating improved antitumor immunity. Our study demonstrates that in vivo reprogramming of T cells through targeted Kv1.3 enhancement can overcome immunosuppressive barriers within the tumor microenvironment and enhance immune-mediated tumor clearance in vivo. This novel approach offers a scalable and cost-effective alternative to ex vivo T cell engineering and holds promise as a therapeutic strategy to improve immunotherapy outcomes in HNSCC and other solid tumors characterized by Kv1.3-dependent immune dysfunctions.

items.title: ERM proteins antagonistically control cancer invasion and metastasis via mechanosensing regulation
items.blurb: Metastasis requires cancer cells to overcome anchorage dependence and rewire mechanosensing pathways. Here, we identify the ERM proteins ezrin, radixin, and moesin as key but antagonistic regulators of breast cancer metastasis. Expression profiling across matched low- and high-metastatic breast cancer models revealed consistent upregulation of all three ERM proteins in highly metastatic cells. Despite this, ezrin depletion reduced colony formation, invasion, and lung metastasis, whereas radixin or moesin depletion enhanced these phenotypes. Loss of radixin or moesin increased ezrin localization at the cell edge, while ezrin depletion reduced membrane-associated moesin, indicating a dynamic balance among ERM proteins. Ezrin depletion also increased focal adhesion size and number, FAK activation, and force transmission to the extracellular matrix, whereas radixin or moesin silencing produced opposite effects. Cellular force magnitude was inversely correlated with invasion, and pharmacological modulation of contractility reverted the effects of ERM depletion. These findings reveal an ERM-dependent mechanosensing checkpoint that regulates metastasis through control of adhesion dynamics and force transmission.

items.title: Gene set selection for classification with single-cell RNA-seq
items.blurb: Marker genes are important for analyzing and interpreting single-cell RNA-seq (scRNAseq) experiments. They are used to identify and categorize cell types and can also be useful for the design of downstream experiments. We present CellSieve, which tackles the problem of finding effective gene sets rather than distilling markers one at a time. While several "combinatorial" approaches to gene set selection have been proposed, we find that our approach, which leverages a combination of multinomial logistic regression and linear programming, is much more effective at finding small gene sets that can classify cell types.

items.title: Flux Transformer learns intracellular metabolic fluxes from isotope labeling and measured reaction rates
items.blurb: Cells convert incoming nutrients into energy and biomass via metabolic fluxes. Quantifying these fluxes involves feeding cells isotope-labeled nutrients, quantifying metabolite labeling patterns, and inverting the labeling data to retrieve the underlying flux distribution. Traditional metabolic flux analysis (MFA) is both computationally expensive and frequently requires manual refinement of the cost function to obtain plausible results. For this reason, MFA has remained inaccessible to non-experts. Here we present Flux Transformer, an AI model that uses reaction-specific attention to integrate isotope-labeling data with available reaction-rate measurements, reconstructing mass-balanced steady-state fluxes. The model is trained on simulated data with added noise and identifies the underlying fluxes from these data more effectively than traditional MFA. Provided experimental data from wild-type and mutant bacteria, yeast, plants, and mammalian T cells, it efficiently and accurately recovers expert-curated MFA fluxes. By making flux analysis accessible, Flux Transformer is poised to accelerate metabolic research and engineering.

items.title: Identifying disease-associated dysbiosis in image-based spatial microbiome via MiSA
items.blurb: Background: Extensive studies have revealed the associations of microbiome dysbiosis with disease through compositional analysis of 16S rRNA amplicon or shotgun metagenomic sequencing data. However, dysbiosis in spatial organization of microbiome inhabiting the body sites and its implication for diseases remain understudied. Recently developed high phylogenetic resolution fluorescence in situ hybridization (HiPR-FISH) is an image-based mapping technology that provides spatial microbiome data at single-cell resolution, which allows for visualizing and quantifying spatial arrangement of microbial cells. Despite the growing availability of such data, no methods have been tailored to studying spatial dysbiosis in image-based microbiome data. Results: Here we introduce MiSA (Microbiome Spatial Aberration), the first statistical framework for identifying disease-associated spatial dysbiosis and the individual taxa that may contribute to it, based on differing degrees of clustering or regularity, i.e., microbial cells being more aggregated or more evenly spaced than expected under complete spatial randomness, between diagnostic groups. In simulations based on a real dataset, MiSA was robust across diverse and noisy spatial configurations, achieving substantially higher statistical power than a method borrowed from spatial proteomics, while controlling type I error at both the individual-taxon and community levels. When applied to an oral biofilm study, MiSA detected peri-implant mucositis-associated spatial dysbiosis at the community level and identified five taxa as potential contributors, including Actinomyces, which showed increased clustering in mucositis. Conclusions: MiSA is a powerful and robust framework for identifying spatial dysbiosis and the contributing taxa in image-based microbiome data, offering new insights into the spatial organization of microbial communities in disease.

items.title: Stress granule transcript contrasts between colorectal cancer compartments depend on scoring and depth
items.blurb: Stress granule (SG) gene-set scores summarize transcription associated with stress-response machinery, but their stability across scoring definitions is uncertain. We compared fibroblast-epithelial expression contrasts for four fixed SG lists in two colorectal cancer single-cell cohorts containing 195,527 cells from 85 donors. Analyses used donor pairing, gene-wise standardized expression, within-cell ranks and raw-count pseudobulk summaries, with tissue and sequencing-depth sensitivities. At least 20 tumor cells per compartment were available for 15 and 29 paired donors. Pseudobulk SG-A contrasts were negative in both cohorts: median differences in mean log2 counts per million were -0.383 (95% confidence interval -0.493 to -0.319) and -0.493 (-0.614 to -0.384). Rank-based SG-B contrasts were also negative in both cohorts. In a post hoc comparison using identical depth-retained cells and weights, the second cohort had positive gene-Z estimates and negative rank-based estimates; the positive estimates did not meet the eight-test false-discovery threshold. Spatial comparisons depended on the fibroblast reference subtype, and the CosMx panel measured only 11 of 27 SG-B genes. RNA-protein correlations varied across genes, while organoid depletion calls were more frequent for selected translation-associated members than for the four core members. These findings establish reproducible relative-expression contrasts under specified definitions and show that their direction can change across scoring and depth conditions. Reporting the scoring definition, retained donor population, depth sensitivity and gene coverage together identifies the contrasts that reproduce and provides a defined basis for testing their relationship to SG formation.

items.title: ALI MEA60: A porous thin-film microelectrode array for air-liquid interface electrophysiology of 3D excitable tissues
items.blurb: Objective: Conventional microelectrode arrays (MEAs) are suboptimal for long-term electrophysiology of three-dimensional (3D) excitable tissues, as limited oxygenation, nutrient diffusion, and tissue-electrode coupling compromise recording stability. Air-liquid interface (ALI) culture mitigates these constraints, but existing ALI MEA platforms are limited in channel count, flexibility, and compatibility with commercial multichannel acquisition systems. We developed and comprehensively characterized a next-generation ALI MEA for standardized, long-term recordings across multiple 3D excitable tissue models. Approach: The novel ALI MEA60 is composed of a porous polyimide membrane that integrates an array of 60 thin film microelectrodes (59 recording, one reference) and a basal perfusion chamber with Luer-lock connectors for controlled medium exchange and pharmacological wash-in/wash-out. It is compatible with the MEA2100-Mini data acquisition system (Multi Channel Systems). We characterized electrode impedance and noise across 41 ALI MEA60 devices, assessed 60-day stability with human iPSC-derived neural spheroids (N = 7 MEAs, 121 recordings) using a standardized longitudinal framework and linear mixed-effects models, and evaluated its versatility through pharmacological assays and recordings from human neural spheroids, brain organoids, ex vivo brain slices, and cardiac organoids. Main results: The platform showed reproducible electrical performance (median impedance 56 kOhms; at 1 kHz) and low noise (approx. 5uV Root Mean Square (RMS) in saline, 10-20 uV in medium), resolving spikes and local field potentials simultaneously. Recording remained stable for at least 60 days, with a stable noise floor and ~85% persistence of initial functional channels. Neural spheroids reproduced the standard qualitative signatures to gabazine, 4-aminopyridine (4-AP), and 6-Cyano-7-nitroquinoxaline-2,3-dione/D-2-amino-5-phosphonovalerate (CNQX/D-AP5), while cardiac organoids showed the expected beta-adrenergic response to isoproterenol. The ALI MEA60 can similarly record signals from human brain slices and organoids without hardware modification. Significance: The ALI MEA60 combines ALI culture, chronic recording stability, standardized pharmacological testing and cross-tissue compatibility in a single ready-to-use platform. It also establishes a reproducible framework for benchmarking long-term electrophysiological performance, thereby supporting disease modelling, drug discovery, organ-on-chip technologies and future chronic 3D electrophysiology systems. Keywords: microelectrode array (MEA); air-liquid interface (ALI); 3D excitable tissues; neural spheroids; cardiac organoids; chronic electrophysiology.

items.title: Sterically Controlled Conformational Gating of Rhodamine Spirolactam Switches for Super-Resolution Imaging
items.blurb: The reversible interconversion of rhodamines between nonfluorescent spirocyclic and fluorescent ring-open states underpins fluorogenic probes and spontaneously blinking dyes for super-resolution imaging. Existing strategies mainly tune the equilibrium between these states through electronic modification, whereas the role of conformational return in ring closure remains less explored. Here, we establish steric regulation of rhodamine spirolactams through amide N-substituents. Bulky substituents generate intramolecular repulsion with the xanthene scaffold, favoring ring opening. Crystallographic observations reveal substantial amide reorientation upon opening, suggesting increased separation between the nitrogen and meso-carbon reaction centers. We propose that substituent-dependent conformational accessibility modulates C-N bond reformation and the lifetime of the emissive state. The tert-butyl-substituted dye 1e exhibits an open-state residence time of 145 ms, despite its lower pKcycl. Calculations also indicate a lower ring-opening barrier for 1e than for less hindered 1a (1.12 vs 1.37 eV). Incorporating this design into HaloTag probes enables SIM, STED, and SMLM imaging. Importantly, N-halo-RBRB enables dual-modal SIM/SMLM imaging with a single fluorophore, integrating the rapid reconstruction of overall cellular architecture by SIM with single-molecule localization information from SMLM. This work identifies sterically modulated conformational accessibility as a design principle for engineering reversible rhodamine switches with tailored imaging capabilities.

items.title: Workflow for Assessing Mass Spectrometer Performance in Shotgun Lipidomics
items.blurb: Reproducible and testable analytical performance of mass spectrometers is critical for inter-laboratory concordance of quantitative lipidomics analyses. However, common instrument readout or analyses of arbitrarily chosen lipid mixtures do not lend themselves to direct comparison between instruments independently configured and operated in different laboratories under in-house settings. We developed and validated the QC Shotgun workflow and web-accessible software that enable rapid testing, evaluation, documentation, and longitudinal monitoring of the performance of high-resolution mass spectrometers in quantitative shotgun lipidomics. Completed in less than 5 minutes, the QC Shotgun test reports 8 relative metric indices that facilitate inter-laboratory comparison and longitudinal assessment of instrument performance and identify deficiencies that are not apparent from instrument readouts. Systematic documentation of instrument status can improve inter-laboratory consistency and interpretation confidence of lipidomics datasets.

items.title: De Novo Design of Miniprotein Binders Targeting the Leptin-Binding Site of the Leptin Receptor
items.blurb: The leptin receptor (LEPR) regulates appetite, energy balance, glucose homeostasis, and neuroendocrine function and is closely associated with obesity, diabetes, and neurological disorders. Activation of LEPR signaling suppresses appetite and promotes energy expenditure, whereas impaired LEPR signaling and leptin resistance are commonly associated with obesity. Accordingly, modulation of LEPR signaling is a potential therapeutic strategy for obesity and related metabolic disorders. In this study, we report the de novo computational design of miniprotein binders targeting the leptin-binding site within the cytokine receptor homology 2 (CRH2) domain of LEPR. Computational screening and biochemical characterization identified the miniprotein binder Mini-19484, which adopted a stable -helical fold and exhibited enhanced resistance to proteolytic degradation. Mini-19484 bound the LEPR CRH2 domain with high affinity, with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 30 nM. Structural analysis of the predicted model and mutagenesis studies revealed that Arg18 of Mini-19484 serves as a critical interaction hotspot for LEPR binding. The predicted binding mode of Mini-19484 differed substantially from that of natural leptin, providing a distinct molecular scaffold for targeting the LEPR CRH2 domain. These findings provide a valuable framework for developing miniprotein-based therapeutics targeting LEPR.

items.title: Wilson disease mechanisms manipulate ATP7B activity
items.blurb: Copper is an essential cofactor for enzymes involved in diverse processes including mitochondrial respiration and the metabolism of neurotransmitters, collagen and melanin. However, its redox activity requires tight homeostatic control. The P-type ATPases ATP7A and ATP7B help deliver copper to cuproenzymes, and ATP7B mediates the excretion of excess copper into bile. Pathogenic ATP7B variants cause Wilson disease (WD), leading to copper accumulation in organs including the liver, kidney, and brain, and to disruption of copper-dependent processes. Current treatments primarily reduce systemic copper levels, while emerging gene therapies aim to restore ATP7B function. A complementary therapeutic strategy would be to rescue dysfunctional ATP7B using pharmacological chaperones, but their development is limited by an insufficient understanding of how WD variants perturb ATP7B structure and function. Here, we present a cryo-EM structure of human ATP7B reconstituted in lipid nanodiscs together with coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, as well as mutagenesis, functional and sequence analyses. We identify a salt bridge (E754-R969), crucial for the transition between inward- and outward-facing conformations, which is abolished by the R969Q disease variant. Additionally, we find a conserved stabilizing cholesterol-binding site severely disrupted by the WD variant W939C. Furthermore, we present new insights into the dynamics of metal binding domains 5 and 6 hinting at a copper relay mechanism in ATP7B. Together, these findings reveal lipid- and domain-mediated mechanisms of ATP7B regulation and explain how specific WD variants disrupt them, providing a structural framework for mutation-directed therapeutic strategies, including pharmacological chaperones.

items.title: Making monkeys of caregivers: Evaluating the use of caregiver behaviour as social enrichment for lab-housed Rhesus and Cynomolgus Macaques
items.blurb: Enrichment is pivotal to captive animal welfare. Social enrichment is of particular importance for social animals who, due to laboratory space or protocols, are not housed in larger groups. The objective of our study was to see if caregivers could act as an additional source of social enrichment to pair-housed research macaques. 5 adult Rhesus (Macaca Mulatta) and 3 adult Cynomolgus macaques (Macaca fascicularis) were enrolled in the study. Every day, for 3 weeks, caregivers would spend 6 minutes interacting with the monkeys during afternoon feeding. Half the monkeys received human behaviour (HB), where the caregivers interacted with the monkeys using human body language and speaking softly. The other half received monkey-like behaviour (MB), in which caregivers would attempt to imitate monkey behaviour, all the while avoiding eye-contact or speaking (both of which may be perceived as aggressive). Our results showed that monkeys were more likely to engage in interactions before feeding, indicating that this may be an ideal time to provide social enrichment. Monkeys from both groups showed a 3.5 {+/-} 1.5 (F54 = 3.34, p = 0.058) decrease in the frequency of cage-directed abnormal behaviours and a 1.2 {+/-} 0.53 (F54 = 2.78, p = 0.067) decrease in the frequency of stereotypic abnormal over the course of the experiment. In addition, all monkeys saw a 12.9 {+/-} 6.1% (F54 = 2.40, p = 0.010) increase in the proportion of time spent interacting positively with cage-mates, including a 10.6 {+/-} 4.78% (F54.1 = 2.47, p = 0.077) increase in time spent grooming. This research contributes to the enhancement of animal care by helping to establish evidence-based guidelines for the proper care of non-human primates in research. It further deepens our understanding of social enrichment provided by humans as a cost-effective way of managing boredom.

items.title: Contrasting plasmid-host associations shape the distribution of enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC) colonization factors
items.blurb: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) causes a substantial burden of diarrhoeal disease, but how its virulence plasmids spread across E. coli populations remains unclear. We generated 479 complete ETEC genomes and combined them with 56 publicly available assemblies to produce the largest plasmid-resolved ETEC collection to date. Clustering of 903 virulence plasmids identified distinct plasmid lineages associated with individual colonization factors (CFs). Some CFs were carried by plasmids confined to a single ETEC lineage, consistent with long-term vertical maintenance, whereas others, including CS23 and CS12, were found on closely related conjugative plasmids distributed across multiple lineages, indicating horizontal transfer. Screening the AllTheBacteria dataset confirmed these patterns and revealed additional plasmid diversity for several CFs. Finally, we identified eight previously undescribed putative adhesion operons on toxin plasmids that may explain CF-negative ETEC isolates. These findings showed that plasmids, rather than bacterial lineages alone, shape the evolution and dissemination of ETEC virulence.

items.title: A conserved dimerization motif squelches transcription
items.blurb: Squelching is an indirect inhibition of transcription that results from redistribution of cofactors away from DNA. Here, we describe a class of Lis homology (LisH)-derived peptides that act as transcriptional squelchers. LisH domains are a highly conserved motif found in 10s of thousands of proteins and are composed of ~30 amino acids in a helix-turn-helix fold. By examining a phylogenetically diverse subset of LisH domains in a synthetic Saccharomyces cerevisiae assay, we identified a small number of hydrophobic residues within the first helix that are required for effective inhibition of reporter expression. In addition, squelching required binding to the general transcriptional cofactor Taf5, a subunit of the TFIID complex. Transcriptome-level impacts were largely correlated in yeast expressing two distinct LisH sequences, consistent with a model that LisH-based squelching results from a shared mechanism of sequestering Taf5. Consistent with that inference, overexpression of Taf5 partially reversed the squelching effect. Given the interest in squelching as a potential area for anti-cancer therapies, we also tested whether our shortest squelching sequence called YC5C-H1 had any effect on the human colorectal cancer cell line HCT-15. In addition to preferentially squelching high expression genes, YC5C-H1 sharply slowed growth of HCT-15 cells.

items.title: Community responses outweigh species-level plasticity in shaping future marine forests
items.blurb: Anthropogenic ocean warming (OW) and acidification (OA) are progressively reshaping marine ecosystems, yet ecosystem-level evidence remains limited. Marine forests are foundational ecosystems that support highly productive and diverse communities. Understanding how macroalgal communities will assemble, perform and persist in future ocean conditions requires integrated evidence capturing concurrent shifts in primary productivity, species interactions, and associated macroalgal community responses. Here, we provide a multi-level approach combining laboratory experiments with field surveys to assess how Mediterranean marine macroalgal forests will respond to future warming and acidification. We used local populations from natural CO2; vents in Panarea (Aeolian Islands, Italy) and present-day pH conditions of the emblematic forest-forming species Ericaria balearica to quantify multi-level responses to future climate drivers. Specifically, we crossed temperature (present day, T+2 C, T+4 C), pH (present day pHT ~ 7.9, low pHT ~7.6), and origin population (ambient vs CO2 vents) in laboratory experiments, where we measured changes in Ericaria biomass and metabolism, as well as herbivory by the sea urchin Paracentrotus lividus. We also assessed in situ community structure by quantifying species-specific percent cover and biomass along a pH gradient. In natural CO2 vents, E. balearica biomass was greater than at ambient sites, and associated macroalgal community composition differed between pH zones. In the laboratory, across the simulated spring-summer warming period, E. balerarica biomass declined similarly in all treatments with no important effect of pH; a marginal signal suggested that vent-origin individuals retained more biomass only under present-day temperature. Sea urchin consumption was reduced under low pH and showed a weaker response to temperature. Overall, we found no clear direct impact of OWxOA on E. balearica performance but significant influence of OA on herbivory and the associated macroalgal community, indicating that ecological processes outweigh the effects at the individual or population level.

items.title: Resource enrichment and utilization underlie widely observed production and biomass scaling relationships
items.blurb: Broadly observed trophic scaling patterns relate the biomass of predators to the biomass of prey, and biomass to productivity. The consistency with which these patterns are observed suggests the existence of governing principles that apply across ecosystems. We present a model for the trophic interaction between phytoplankton and zooplankton that produces the scaling patterns as an emergent property of resource enrichment without invoking the influence of phenotypic or genotypic diversity on system structure. Using formulations with broad empirical support, the model incorporates processes that are common to all ecosystems: resource enrichment, feeding, growth, maintenance, and mortality. Thus, our interpretation of widely observed scaling relationships provides constraints for models that quantify the coupling between ecosystem structure and elemental cycles across terrestrial and aquatic environments.

items.title: EHMT1 and EHMT2 Control the Timing of Cortical Neurogenesis Through H3K9me2-Dependent and -Independent Mechanisms
items.blurb: The precise timing of neural progenitor differentiation and cell fate specification is critical for establishing the size and cellular diversity of the cerebral cortex. However, how chromatin regulators control the temporal progression of neurogenesis remains poorly understood. Here we investigate the cooperative roles of Euchromatic Histone Lysine Methyltransferases 1 and 2 (EHMT1 and EHMT2) in mouse cortical neurogenesis. We demonstrate that EHMT1- and EHMT2-mediated H3K9me2 deposition is dispensable for H3K9me3, and that these histone marks occupy distinct chromatin regions. Combined loss of EHMT1 and EHMT2 reduces neural progenitor proliferation, promotes differentiation, and disrupts the transition from deep- to upper-layer neurogenesis, resulting in microcephaly and altered neuronal subtype composition in the postnatal cortex. We further show that EHMT2 directly regulates genes involved in neurogenesis and upper-layer neuron specification through both transcriptional repression and activation. Moreover, EHMT1 and EHMT2 suppress the premature expression of synaptic genes in neural progenitors through complementary mechanisms involving H3K9me2-associated chromatin compaction and H3K9me2-independent silencing in cooperation with PRDM16. Together, these findings establish EHMT1 and EHMT2 as central regulators of the temporal control of cortical neurogenesis and reveal molecular mechanisms that may contribute to the pathogenesis of Kleefstra syndrome.

items.title: Confocal Live-Cell Imaging Under Ultralow Irradiance Using Superconducting Transition-Edge Sensor
items.blurb: Confocal laser scanning fluorescence microscopy (CLSFM) is widely used for three-dimensional live-cell imaging. However, high irradiance is required to overcome dark counts in photodetectors, often leading to observation bias. In this study, we examine whether a CLSFM system equipped with a virtually dark-count-free superconducting transition-edge sensor (TES) can enable live-cell imaging under low irradiance, thereby mitigating observation bias. Using green fluorescent protein-tagged HeLa cells, we determined the minimum laser power required for live-cell imaging and demonstrated suppression of photobleaching and cell-division arrest during long-term observation. Innate fluorescence signature analysis revealed that TES-CLSFM could discriminate between two oleaginous yeast species with different lipid productivities at ca. 1/400 the irradiance required by conventional CLSFM. These results establish TES-CLSFM as a minimally invasive imaging modality for the quantitative physiological assessment of living cells.

items.title: Revealing the platelet transcriptome using Siphon-seq: a sensitive, purity-aware method for RNA-sequencing
items.blurb: Platelet transcriptomics is limited by the exceptionally low RNA content of platelets and by disproportionate contributions from contaminating cells to bulk RNA-sequencing libraries. We developed Siphon-seq, an approach that deliberately overloads independently barcoded single-cell partitions to increase aggregate platelet RNA input, then computationally identifies and removes partitions containing contaminating RNA after sequencing. Applied to 34 healthy human donors, Siphon-seq increased platelet-marker representation, depleted leukocyte and erythrocyte transcripts, and removed contamination-associated inter-donor transcriptional structure. We defined a 3,436-gene core platelet transcriptome that was strongly related to megakaryocyte expression. However, megakaryocyte transcription did not fully explain the platelet transcriptome, which had specific pathways systematically enriched or depleted that were obscured by leukocyte contamination. These findings were confirmed in an independent cohort and were associated with protein detection in two platelet proteome resources. In a pilot human sepsis cohort, Siphon-seq reduced transcripts associated with leukocytes to reveal increased platelet-associated pathway signals. These contaminating immune pathways were also enriched in samples analyzed by bulk RNA-seq from an independent sepsis cohort, most strongly in the stratum with the highest estimated leukocyte burden. Combined, these results reveal that RNA-level contamination can alter both transcriptome structure and biological inference, and that Siphon-seq bridges the sensitivity-purity tradeoff that has limited platelet RNA sequencing, enabling sensitive, purity-aware studies of platelet biology in health and disease.

items.title: STL1267 alters HIF-1α and REV-ERBα localization and transcriptional responses in CoCl2-treated HeLa cells
items.blurb: Background: REV-ERB nuclear receptors regulate gene expression and cellular metabolism, but their role in the response to hypoxia-associated stress remains unclear. We examined how the REV-ERB agonist STL1267 affects protein distribution and gene expression in HeLa cells exposed to cobalt chloride (CoCl2). Methods and Results: Immunofluorescence microscopy and RNA sequencing were used to compare vehicle-treated controls, cells exposed to CoCl2 plus vehicle, and cells exposed to CoCl2 plus STL1267. Representative images showed stronger nuclear HIF-1 staining after CoCl2 exposure. Nuclear staining was less pronounced with STL1267, while REV-ERB showed more extranuclear staining. CoCl2 exposure altered 267 genes, and STL1267 treatment during CoCl2 exposure altered 132 genes at a false discovery rate below 0.05. STL1267 increased ATF4 expression alongside genes involved in amino-acid synthesis and one-carbon metabolism, including ASNS, PHGDH, PSAT1, PSPH and MTHFD2. CTH and CHAC1 also increased, highlighting changes in sulfur-amino-acid metabolism and glutathione turnover. Among the genes induced by CoCl2, CA9, BNIP3 and LDHA decreased with STL1267, whereas HK2, PDK1 and VEGFA did not change significantly. Conclusions: STL1267 selectively reshapes hypoxia-associated gene expression and induces an ATF4-associated metabolic transcriptional program in CoCl2-treated HeLa cells, alongside qualitative changes in HIF-1 and REV-ERB distribution. These findings identify a potential connection between protein compartmentalization and metabolic stress responses, providing a basis for investigating how REV-ERB ligands influence cellular adaptation to oxygen limitation.

items.title: Palmitic acid promotes glomerulosclerosis via TGF-β1 upregulation in podocytes
items.blurb: Podocytes are terminally differentiated visceral epithelial cells of the glomerulus and play a vital role in renal filtration. Nevertheless, they are vulnerable to several insults in obesity and metabolic syndrome. Obesity-related glomerulopathy (ORG) is characterized by podocyte hypertrophy, reduced podocyte density, and secondary focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS). However, how lipid overload, particularly palmitic acid (PA), whose plasma levels are frequently elevated in obesity, injures podocytes remains incompletely understood. Human podocytes were exposed to PA (100 M for 24 hours), and we assessed lipid accumulation, WT1 expression and promoter activity, TGF-{beta}1 signaling, and cell-cycle regulators. PA induced lipid droplet accumulation and increased WT1 expression in podocytes. Concurrently, PA treated podocytes showed cytoskeletal aberrations, loss of podocyte structural genes (podocin, nephrin and synaptopodin) and TGF-{beta}1/Smad2 axis causes upregulation of fibronectin, collagen, and -SMA. Similarly, mice fed a high-fat diet (HFD) for 16 weeks exhibited TGF- {beta}1 activation in podocyte enriched glomeruli together with glomerulosclerosis, impaired kidney function, and podocyte loss. In both models, Cyclin D1, Cyclin B1, CDK4, p53, and p21 were increased. Notably, ~30% of PA-treated podocytes were binucleated, yet podocyte number did not increase. Lipotoxic stress was associated with concurrent induction of WT1 and TGF-{beta}1, loss of the podocyte phenotype, and abortive cell-cycle re-entry accompanied by binucleation and podocyte loss. These findings point to a WT1-TGF-{beta}1-cell-cycle axis as a potential contributor to ORG and a candidate therapeutic target. Whether WT1 directly regulates TGF-{beta}1 remains to be determined.

items.title: Kinesin-1 selectivity for stable microtubules is mediated by MAP7D1's recognition of expanded lattices
items.blurb: Microtubules are organized into functionally distinct subsets that differ in stability, post-translational modifications (PTMs) and lattice spacing, but what defines these subsets and governs selective binding of motors and microtubule-associated proteins (MAPs) to specific subsets has remained unclear. Here, we demonstrate that the preferential motility of the motor protein Kinesin-1 along stable, long-lived microtubules depends on microtubule lattice spacing and MAP7 family members. Using Kinesin-1 truncations and MAP7 family depletions, we show that Kinesin-1 subset selectivity is not specified by its motor domain, but instead requires its coiled-coil 1 region, which mediates MAP7 binding. While depletion of all MAP7 proteins abolishes Kinesin-1 motility, loss of MAP7D1 alone results in non-selective motility, identifying MAP7D1 as the key determinant of selectivity. Using knock-out cells lacking detyrosinated and acetylated microtubules, we find that MAP7D1 enrichment on stable microtubule subsets depends on lattice structure rather than PTMs, whereas in vitro reconstitution assays directly demonstrate that MAP7D1 preferentially binds expanded microtubule lattices characteristic of long-lived microtubules. Together, our results establish microtubule lattice conformation as a key determinant of cellular microtubule subset identity and selective binding of MAPs.

items.title: A minimal common core and dynamic protein associations orchestrate nuclear mRNP maturation
items.blurb: How nuclear mRNAs are selectively packaged into ribonucleoprotein particles (mRNPs) is fundamental to elucidating the mechanisms that govern gene expression. Here, we interrogate nuclear mRNP maturation in S. cerevisiae by combining a proteomic (34 baits) and transcriptomic (18 baits) affinity-purification survey with sequential purification of individual MS2-tagged nuclear transcripts at successive stages of maturation. Contrary to the prevailing models in which nuclear mRNAs are extensively coated with a stable complement of proteins, we find that they share a minimal core of Yra1p and Pab1p, together with a more dynamically associated cap-binding complex. Most other factors associate transiently and transcript-selectively, assembling as pre-assembled, stage-specific modules. The minimal core is invariant to promoter, coding sequence and transcript length, whereas intron class, rather than intron presence alone, determines spliceosome composition. The breadth of factor association further tracks promoter class and proximity to chromatin-domain boundaries, linking mRNP biogenesis to genome organization.

items.title: RPAP3 impairs TRBP-mediated translation of TAR-containing RNAs and FTSJ3 recruitment onto the HIV-1 genomic RNA
items.blurb: The interaction between TRBP and RPAP3, which is mutually exclusive from that between TRBP and Dicer, revealed a possible role for RPAP3 in the regulation of miRNA activity. Besides miRNA processing and/or function, TRBP is involved in promoting the expression of TAR-containing transcripts, and to impede innate immune system from sensing HIV-1 in infected cells by recruiting the cellular 2'-O-methyltransferase FTSJ3 onto the viral RNA. Here, we show that RPAP3 prevents the TRBP stimulatory effect on the translation of TAR-containing reporters, both in vitro and in cellulo, without affecting TRBP's ability to bind to the TAR. We also observe that virion production is increased in RPAP3 depleted cells. Additionally, we show that TRBP directly recruits the methyltransferase FTSJ3, and that RPAP3 inhibits this ability. These observations open new avenues for possible novel therapeutics strategies aimed at hindering TRBP pro-viral functions, via novel regulation mechanisms involving RPAP3.

items.title: Tissue-specific genomic and transcriptomic dynamics of the OsHV-1 lytic cycle in the Pacific oyster Magallana gigas revealed by long-read sequencing
items.blurb: Ostreid herpesvirus 1 (OsHV-1) causes recurrent mass mortality of juvenile Pacific oysters (Magallana gigas) worldwide, yet its lytic cycle remains poorly characterized in vivo. In the absence of a permissive cell line, most studies have relied on intramuscular injection, which bypasses the natural route of infection, or on primary haemocyte cultures, which cannot capture tissue-level host-virus interactions. In addition, gene expression studies have relied on short-read sequencing, which fragments transcription units and cannot resolve complex transcriptional architectures. Long-read sequencing has recently revealed abundant overlapping, antisense and polycistronic transcripts in other herpesviruses, but whether OsHV-1 shares this complexity, and how its transcriptional program varies across host tissues during natural infection, remains unknown. Here, we exposed naive oysters to OsHV-1 by bath exposure and combined long-read genomic and transcriptomic sequencing of gills, mantle, digestive gland and adductor muscle at increasing levels of infection. OsHV-1 genomes were assembled directly from infected tissues, and intra-host viral diversity was structured by host rather than tissue. We identified 410 unspliced viral transcripts, including overlapping, antisense and polycistronic transcripts. The viral transcriptional program was largely conserved across tissues and resembled that previously described in haemocytes in vitro. In the host, infection triggered a response shared by all tissues, but earlier and stronger in the gills and mantle. Together, these results provide the first long-read view of the OsHV-1 lytic cycle in its natural host.

items.title: Genomic and phenotypic characterisation of Penicillium melinii, a plant growth-promoting root endophyte that remains effective under salt stress
items.blurb: Penicillium melinii isolate 2 is a root endophyte of Arabidopsis thaliana that promotes the growth of different plant species, but the genetic basis of this activity remains unknown. Here we combined Oxford Nanopore long reads and Illumina short reads to obtain a high-quality, near-chromosome-level assembly of 29.39 Mb in six nuclear scaffolds, two of them telomere-capped at both ends (97.6% complete BUSCOs), together with, to our knowledge, the first complete mitochondrial genome reported for the species (26,730 bp). Annotation predicted 9,566 protein-coding genes. Compared with two other plant growth-promoting Penicillium species, P. bilaiae and P. citrinum, the isolate encodes fewer carbohydrate-active enzymes, biosynthetic gene clusters and candidate effectors, pointing to an overall reduction of the secreted repertoire. In vitro, the isolate grew significantly above the control on 63 of 95 carbon sources, mainly carbohydrates, and was positive for 7 of 11 plant growth-promoting traits: siderophore production, phosphate and zinc solubilisation, ammonia release, and urease, proteolytic and lipolytic activities. Radial growth was unaffected by NaCl up to 150 mM and persisted at 1 M, whereas conidiation was more salt-sensitive. On medium containing 100 mM NaCl, inoculation increased Arabidopsis shoot fresh weight and root system growth. Genome mining identified candidate genes for these traits. Together, these results provide a genomic and phenotypic basis for evaluating P. melinii isolate 2 as an inoculant for saline soils and identify candidate determinants for functional validation.

items.title: Defining host factors required for dengue virus NS1-induced endothelial hyperpermeability and endothelial glycocalyx layer disruption
items.blurb: Dengue virus (DENV) is a mosquito-borne positive-sense RNA virus belonging to the Flaviviridae family that poses a significant threat to global health. Clinical manifestations of DENV infection range from febrile to severe disease characterized by vascular leakage. The secreted DENV nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) contributes to endothelial dysfunction through interactions with endothelial cells, leading to disruption of the endothelial glycocalyx and intercellular junction complexes (IJC). However, host factors required for NS1-triggered endothelial dysfunction are not well understood. It is also unclear if NS1 highjacks different host factors and signaling pathways for glycocalyx and IJC disruption. To address these questions, we used a targeted genetic approach to identify host factors required either for NS1-triggered endothelial glycocalyx layer (EGL) disruption, as assessed by immunofluorescence assays, or for IJC disruption, as measured by transendothelial electrical resistance. After demonstrating the decoupled nature of EGL and IJC disruption in our models, we genetically depleted host factors with known roles in regulating endothelial barrier function and/or involvement in NS1 pathogenesis, including heparanase, cathepsin L, sialidases, and the PI3K/AKT/mTOR and {beta}-catenin signaling pathways. Our results reveal a complex genetic landscape where NS1-induced disruption of EGL and IJCs involves both unique and shared host factors. Further, our data identify a direct role for {beta}-catenin in NS1-induced endothelial dysfunction in vitro and in vivo. Overall, this work advances understanding of host factors required for DENV NS1-triggered endothelial dysfunction, revealing distinct intracellular pathways that are highjacked by NS1 to modulate barrier function, thus providing new insights into dengue-associated vascular leak.

items.title: Genomic reassessment of Enterobacter species and subspecies
items.blurb: Enterobacter species are opportunistic pathogens whose identification is complicated by closely related lineages and changing species nomenclature. We reassessed 1,074 public genomes using average nucleotide identity (ANI), type-strain comparisons and phylogenies based on conserved markers, genome alignments and k-mers. Among 1,070 genomes included in the classification comparison, 123 changed species or subspecies membership relative to NCBI labels, 499 changed names following revisions to species boundaries or ranks, and 69 previously unnamed genomes received species assignments. The oharae, steigerwaltii, xiangfangensis and hoffmannii lineages formed an expanded Enterobacter xiangfangensis, separate from the lineage containing the E. hormaechei type. We propose five transferred combinations: E. xiangfangensis subsp. oharae comb. nov., E. xiangfangensis subsp. steigerwaltii comb. nov., E. xiangfangensis subsp. hoffmannii comb. nov., E. roggenkampii subsp. quasiroggenkampii comb. nov. and E. chengduensis subsp. rongchengensis comb. nov. We also describe the corresponding type subspecies, E. xiangfangensis subsp. xiangfangensis comb. nov., E. roggenkampii subsp. roggenkampii comb. nov. and E. chengduensis subsp. chengduensis comb. nov., and emend the descriptions of E. xiangfangensis and E. hormaechei. E. dykesii and E. quasimori are treated as later heterotypic synonyms of E. asburiae and E. mori, respectively. Within E. xiangfangensis subsp. hoffmannii, we define 25 genomic groups (genomovars) at 99.5% ANI. Conflicting tree relationships leave the position of E. ludwigii and the branching order of the hoffmannii-associated types unresolved. We developed Pterobacter to apply the revised classifications to assemblies, using alignment-based ANI near the species boundary and withholding assignments when the reference evidence is insufficient.

items.title: FOLR2 Identifies Functionally Distinct Decidual Macrophage Populations that Coordinate Immune and Tissue Remodelling During Human Labour
items.blurb: The initiation of human labour remains incompletely understood, although mounting evidence implicates decidual macrophages in this process. Despite this, macrophage heterogeneity remains poorly defined, with current macrophage classification systems, including M1/M2, failing to capture their biological diversity. Here, we investigate whether macrophage differentiation state, defined by expression of the tissue residency marker FOLR2, provides a more informative framework for characterising human decidual macrophages at term. RNA sequencing and flow cytometry identified FOLR2- and FOLR2+ macrophages as transcriptionally and phenotypically distinct populations. FOLR2- macrophages displayed features consistent with recently recruited monocyte-derived cells and were characterised by enrichment of inflammatory and leukocyte recruitment pathways, with greater expression of IL-8 and CCL5 than FOLR2 macrophages. In contrast, FOLR2 macrophages expressed higher levels of MHC class II molecules, CCL2, IL-6, MMP9 and MMP19, and demonstrated the capacity to degrade collagen in fetal membrane explants. Monocyte and macrophage numbers peaked during early labour in the decidua parietalis, accompanied by increased CCL5 expression, whereas FOLR2+ macrophage expression of MMP9 was highest prior to labour. These findings suggest that decidual macrophage heterogeneity is best understood through differentiation state rather than M1/M2 polarisation and point to complementary roles for FOLR2- and FOLR2 macrophages in leukocyte recruitment, tissue remodelling and the local adaptations required for labour initiation and progression.

items.title: At base of ocean food chain, scientists uncover impacts of a changing atmosphere
items.blurb: Much of the concern about elevated levels of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere focuses on its effects on global warming as a greenhouse gas. But up to 30% of emitted carbon dioxide is absorbed by the oceans, where it reacts with water to lower pH and leads to ocean acidification, which has enormous effects on the chemistry and biology of marine ecosystems.

items.title: The 12th‑century Chinese poet who was among the first to explore the inner lives of cats
items.blurb: If you're reading this, then your media feed, like mine, is probably full of cats.

items.title: More than meets the eye: Refugee reception in eastern Germany can vary by group composition
items.blurb: Imagine a group of newcomers in your local area. Would you expect your neighbors to welcome them or react with reluctance? Would it make a difference how many men and women were in the group, or whether they appeared white or nonwhite?

items.title: Engineered gel controls particle release to help injured spinal cord cells recover in lab
items.blurb: Researchers at the FAMU-FSU College of Engineering have developed a gel that delivers therapeutic particles to injured spinal cord cells, a potential step toward new treatments for spinal cord injuries.

items.title: Turning food waste into insect feed poses only low mad cow disease risk
items.blurb: Insects can convert food waste and by-products from the food industry (such as unsold ready meals or slaughter by-products) into ingredients for animal feed. In this way, they can contribute to the transition toward a circular food production system, in which what would otherwise be wasted is reused. However, these waste streams may contain animal proteins that pose a risk of transmitting diseases such as bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), also known as mad cow disease. For this reason, rearing insects on waste streams containing animal proteins is not permitted in the European Union.

items.title: The Gulf's oil-eating microbes lay in wait before Deepwater Horizon spill, frozen samples suggest
items.blurb: A year before the Deepwater Horizon spill, a NOAA crew scooped up seawater from the Gulf and froze it. Sixteen years later, FIU biologist Shen Jean Lim tested it only to discover the microbes that devoured much of the oil in 2010 were nowhere to be found in 2009. So where did they come from?

items.title: Lasers near physical limits of miniaturization open possibilities for tracking life at the nanoscale
items.blurb: From tracking how cancer develops to exploring how the brain works, scientists need ways to observe biological processes at increasingly smaller scales. Beyond tracking how cells move and interact, researchers need to understand how tiny structures within cells, including organelles and molecular complexes, behave and change over time. However, identifying and tracking these microscopic targets individually remains a major challenge.

items.title: New model identifies priority areas for large-scale ecological restoration in Chile
items.blurb: Researchers from Chile's Institute of Ecology and Biodiversity (IEB) have developed a multiobjective model to identify priority areas for large-scale ecological restoration in Chile, South America. The tool integrates four ecological objectives: reducing species extinction risk, prioritizing carbon stocks, restoring riparian areas and assessing ecological feasibility. The findings show that including ecological feasibility changes restoration priorities, while 80.4% of the selected areas contribute to more than one ecological objective. By identifying areas where different priorities overlap, the model can help guide strategic restoration planning and support better-informed conservation decisions amid growing environmental challenges and limited resources.

items.title: New daisy genus named after botanist
items.blurb: Te Whare Wānanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury (UC) botanist professor Pieter Pelser has been recognized with one of the highest honors in taxonomy, with a newly established South American daisy genus named Pelseria in acknowledgment of his decades-long contribution to studying the family tree of plants.

items.title: New Asian flying frog species identified in Indonesia
items.blurb: In the lush mountain rainforests of Indonesia, researchers have identified a new species of Asian flying frog with distinctive physical features, calls and unusual egg-laying habits. The discovery is described in a paper published in the journal Zootaxa by scientists from Museum Zoologicum Bogoriense in Indonesia, the University of California, Davis, and other collaborators.

items.title: Extreme cold preserves passion fruit's vitamin C, but not all of its antioxidants
items.blurb: Passion fruit can travel thousands of kilometers before it reaches international markets. Along the way, one of the food industry's biggest challenges is making sure its nutritional qualities survive processing, storage and transport.

items.title: Optimized supercomputer workflow accelerates protein-structure prediction
items.blurb: A Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL)-led team has harnessed the power of El Capitan to accelerate generation of predicted protein structures, drastically reducing the computing time required and opening new possibilities for drug discovery, biological research and national security applications.

items.title: Repurposed battery molecules drive key chemical reactions where oil meets water
items.blurb: The process of producing essential medicines and fine chemicals has long been powered by reactions involving intense heat, heavy-metal catalysts and hazardous hydrogen gas. Now, a team of Harvard chemists and engineers has demonstrated that these critical transformations can be driven cleanly by electricity, right at the boundary where oil and water meet.

items.title: Two proteins key to cellulose synthase trafficking and cell wall formation identified
items.blurb: A new study has identified Arabidopsis SNARE proteins VAMP726 and VAMP725 as key components of the trafficking of cellulose synthase (CESA), helping support the formation of both primary and secondary cell walls.

items.title: New platform improves accuracy of molecular counting in RNA-sequencing
items.blurb: The open-source platform, called UMIche (pronounced "you-me-kay"), is described in a new study published in Nature Communications. It addresses a common challenge in RNA-sequencing, where errors during sequencing can lead to inaccurate measurements of gene expression.

items.title: Gut microbiomes of endangered primates reveal hidden toll of habitat loss
items.blurb: As rainforests around the world are cleared for agriculture, livestock grazing, timber harvesting and development, habitat loss is pushing an increasing number of species toward extinction.

items.title: Rapid-scan satellite data offer clues to typhoon intensity
items.blurb: Between 1970 and 2019, tropical cyclones killed nearly 780,000 people worldwide and caused approximately $1.4 trillion in economic losses. As coastal populations continue to grow and climate continues to change, accurate forecasting is essential for saving lives and reducing economic damage.

items.title: GTA V flood simulations reveal how rising seas could reshape Los Santos
items.blurb: Grand Theft Auto V is one of the world's best-known video games. It is set in Los Santos, and although the city is fictional, its landscape and urban structure are modeled very closely on the American city of Los Angeles. Researchers from the Alfred Wegener Institute and the University of Potsdam have explored whether this virtual representation is detailed enough to realistically depict the consequences of a potential rise in sea levels and make them approachable.

items.title: Study uncovers molecular mechanism underlying lip-related floral organ curvature in slipper orchids
items.blurb: A research team from the South China Botanical Garden (SCBG) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences has uncovered a molecular regulatory mechanism that contributes to the development of curved floral organs associated with the distinctive lips of orchids, offering new insights into the development and evolution of floral forms in orchids. The study was published in New Phytologist on Nov. 6.
