items.title: Prefoldin facilitates the action of FACT on macroH2A1-containing chromatin during transcription elongation
items.blurb: Prefoldin is one of the chaperone complexes that participate in protein homeostasis. Although it was initially described as a co-translational cochaperon that captures newly synthesized polypeptides and facilitates their folding by transferring them to class II chaperonins, nuclear functions have also been reported, including its contribution to transcription elongation and chromatin dynamics from budding yeast to mammalian cells. In this work, we have performed a proteomic search for prefoldin interactors in chromatin. Among others, we detected its physical association to FACT, the main histone chaperon that operates during transcription elongation. Lack of prefoldin provokes phenotypes associated to FACT perturbation, like chromatin-integrity defects in transcribed gene bodies, and derepression of cryptic transcription. It also leads to the specific alteration of FACT transcriptional dynamics in prefoldin-regulated genes. Lack of prefoldin also provokes co-transcriptional defects in histone dynamics, particularly in the eviction of macroH2A1, being this non-canonical histone a prefoldin-interactor itself. Finally, we show that these physical and functional connections with FACT and macroH2A1 respond to a single molecular phenomenon, and propose a model in which prefoldin would play a bridging role, enabling FACT to drive co-transcriptional eviction of macroH2A1-containing nucleosomes.

items.title: Semi-stability and unfolding of a KH domain modulate RNA binding and functions of MEX3A
items.blurb: MEX3A is essential for binding to Ago2/miR-126-5p and inhibition of apoptosis in endothelial cells implicated in cardiovascular health. Here, we discovered that the KH1 domain within the RNA binding region of MEX3A exists in equilibrium with an unfolded conformation. Using NMR spectroscopy and biophysical analysis, we dissect the KH1 folding kinetics and show that increased KH1 stability correlates with higher RNA affinity. The unfolded state of KH1 enables phosphorylation of T162, locking the domain in the unfolded conformation and enables recognition by 14-3-3 {zeta}. Residues in MEX3A KH1 that reduce its stability are located outside the RNA-binding interface and are evolutionary selected compared to human MEX3 paralogs. Semi-stability of KH domains in MEX3A and other multi-KH proteins may provide a general mechanism to tune RNA binding, enable phosphorylation and regulate biological function.

items.title: The dynamic expressome of Pseudomonas putida: condition-dependent remodelling of the RNA polymerase interactome
items.blurb: As in many bacteria, the 2{beta}{beta}'{omega} core RNA polymerase (RNAP) of Pseudomonas putida interacts in vivo with sigma factors, transcriptional regulators and auxiliary proteins whose relative abundance varies with the physiological state. Here, we used an in vivo immunocapture approach to examine condition-dependent changes in the RNAP interactome of P. putida KT2440. His-, Myc- and E-tags were separately introduced at the C-terminus of RpoC ({beta}'), a permissive, surface-exposed site accessible to cognate antibodies. Myc-tagged RNAP complexes were immunocaptured with magnetic beads and analyzed by LC-ESI-MS/MS and computational methods. The results revealed condition-dependent association of the RNAP core (RpoA, RpoB, RpoC and RpoZ) with distinct pools of sigma factors, as well as ribosomal proteins, RNA-processing factors and metabolic enzymes. Nutrient starvation, nutrient-rich growth and high temperature altered the composition and relative representation of RNAP-associated proteins. Despite the limited physiological conditions examined, our results support a model in which RNAP acts as a dynamic organizational hub of the bacterial expressome, integrating transcription with translation, RNA maturation and central metabolism.

items.title: Taxogenomic resolution of the 16SrIII (X-disease) group: elevation of Candidatus Phytoplasma pruni-related strains to species rank and proposal of three novel Candidatus species Candidatus Phytoplasma caryae sp. nov., Candidatus Phytoplasma conii sp. nov. and Candidatus Phytoplasma lactucae sp. nov.
items.blurb: Alongside the proposal of the taxon Candidatus Phytoplasma pruni for 16SrIII (X-Disease) group, the designation Candidatus Phytoplasma pruni-related strains was proposed for strains that were closely related to the taxon based on multilocus sequence characterization. However, recent genome-based studies have created taxonomic ambiguity by either assigning related strains directly to the taxon Ca. P. pruni or separating them into more than one genomic cluster without formal taxonomic classification or proposing new taxon for new divergent strains. In this study, we sequenced genomes of the pecan bunchy top phytoplasma (PBT), previously designated a Ca. P. pruni-related strain, initially to confirm the pathogen in an Oklahoma pecan orchard. Phylogenomic comparisons with previously sequenced Candidatus Phytoplasma pruni strains revealed four well-supported taxonomic groups based on average nucleotide identity, digital DNA-DNA hybridization, and phylogenetic analyses, with different host ecologies consistent with International Research Programme on Comparative Mycoplasmology (IRPCM) guidelines for assigning new taxon. Accordingly, we propose a reclassification of Ca. P. pruni and related strains into four species: Candidatus Phytoplasma pruni, representing the taxon associated with X-disease phytoplasma; three proposed new Candidatus species including Candidatus Phytoplasma caryae sp. nov, Candidatus Phytoplasma conii sp. nov and Candidatus Phytoplasma lactucae sp. nov. The study provides comparative-genomic insights into these taxonomic groups that support their evolution.

items.title: HDAC1/2 maintain TERT mRNA stability in TERT-rearranged neuroblastoma
items.blurb: Genomic TERT locus rearrangements define an aggressive high-risk neuroblastoma subgroup characterized by enhancer hijacking, high-level TERT expression and continuous telomerase activation. Although these structural alterations supply a strong transcriptional drive, the post-transcriptional mechanisms preserving TERT mRNA presence remain incompletely understood. We identified histone deacetylases 1 and 2 (HDAC1/2) as essential post-transcriptional guardians of TERT mRNA stability in TERT-rearranged neuroblastoma. Pharmacological inhibition or RNAi-mediated depletion of HDAC1 and HDAC2, but not HDACs 3-11, rapidly downregulated TERT transcript levels and suppressed telomerase enzymatic activity. Transcript decay kinetics following transcriptional arrest with actinomycin D confirmed that HDAC1/2 blockade accelerates TERT mRNA decay, reducing transcript half-life by 30-47%. High-resolution ChIP-seq profiling across the translocation breakpoint demonstrated HDAC inhibition does not alter local chromatin accessibility. Array-based DNA methylation profiling showed only a mild, non-specific global reduction in CpG island methylation upon panobinostat exposure and no focal correlation with TERT transcript loss across the breakpoint locus. Depleting TERT mRNA via HDAC1/2 inhibition dismantled a core 50-gene TERT-associated oncogenic expression network. Ectopic re-expression of TERT cDNA partially rescued cellular viability and normalized expression of key signature genes despite continuous HDAC inhibition. HDAC1/2 inhibition significantly attenuated tumor growth, reduced intratumor TERT expression and prolonging overall survival in both preventive and therapeutic TERT-rearranged xenograft mouse models. Our data establish a post-transcriptional rather than transcriptional mode of TERT regulation and confirm tumor suppression is partly driven by depleting TERT transcripts, uncovering a HDAC1/2 dependency in TERT-driven neuroblastoma. We provide a molecular rationale for therapeutic strategies disrupting HDAC1/2-mediated TERT mRNA stabilization.

items.title: From Calcium-dependent currents to Multitarget Therapy: A Pharmacological Strategy for Glioblastoma
items.blurb: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive primary brain tumor with limited treatment options and substantial interpatient heterogeneity. Ion transport and cell-volume regulation may represent pharmacological vulnerabilities in glioma stem cells (GSCs). Here, we characterized membrane currents in patient-derived GSCs, identifying a calcium-dependent anion conductance consistent with volume-regulated anion channels (VRACs) and an inward current consistent with Na+/Ca++ exchanger exchanger (NCX) activity. Based on these findings, we investigated individual compounds and developed a multitarget cocktail comprising niflumic acid (NFA), bumetanide (BTN), and R-ketorolac (R-K) to target complementary mechanisms involved in ion homeostasis, cell-volume regulation, and cellular dynamics. The cocktail affected cell viability and mechanical properties and showed synergistic effects in U87 cells and patient-derived GSCs with similar electrophysiological profiles. Treatment did not measurably alter spontaneous activity in cultured hippocampal neurons but caused substantial HMC3 cytotoxicity. Encapsulation in transferrin-functionalized liposomes attenuated HMC3 toxicity while preserving activity against glioblastoma cells, suggesting a potential strategy to improve treatment selectivity. Further pharmacological studies identified a potential vulnerability associated with NCX activity, although its contribution to cytotoxicity remains unclear. Overall, our findings highlight electrophysiological heterogeneity in patient-derived GSCs and support further investigation of ion transport as a therapeutic target in GBM. Combining multitarget pharmacology with targeted drug delivery may help address heterogeneous treatment responses, although further studies are needed to establish the underlying mechanisms, safety, and vivo efficacy.

items.title: statLens enables accurate and interpretable statistical intelligence
items.blurb: Diverse existing approaches and analyses of large-scale biomedical omics datasets along with the complexity of the corresponding statistical analytical workflows pose challenges to the direct application of large language models (LLMs) to data analysis tasks. We present statLens, a model-agnostic AI-driven statistical intelligence framework that integrates LLMs, code and human review. We demonstrate statLens using differential expression analysis across heterogeneous biomedical data as a use case. On 102 benchmark tasks from 74 datasets across six omics modalities, statLens maintained consistently high accuracy (92.5--95.0%) across seven language models and outperformed LLM-only inference (17.5--46.8%), whereas autonomous-agent accuracy varied widely (58.7--99.5%). We also showed that statLens substantially improved the accuracy of the four small language models (92.5--94.4%) over autonomous agents (58.7--92.2%) and LLM-only inference (17.5--43.5%). By decomposing analytical workflows into complementary tasks for code, LLMs and human experts, statLens provides an integrated framework for more accurate, interpretable and reproducible AI-assisted data analysis, particularly in complex omics settings.

items.title: SpaceMACE: Spatially-Aware Tumour Cell Annotation for Spatial Transcriptomics
items.blurb: Accurate discrimination between tumour and non-tumour cells is essential for interpreting spatial transcriptomics data and identifying spatially resolved therapeutic targets. Existing tumour-cell annotation approaches were primarily developed for single-cell RNA sequencing and do not explicitly incorporate the spatial organization of cells. Here, we introduce SpaceMACE, an extension of the MACE tumour-cell annotation framework for sequencing-based and imaging-based spatial transcriptomics. SpaceMACE first combines reference-based cell-type classification with copy-number-variation-based tumour classification. The resulting consensus annotations are subsequently refined using spatial proximity and gene-expression similarity. We evaluated SpaceMACE across multiple spatial transcriptomics platforms, including Stereo-seq, Visium HD, CosMx and Xenium, and across colorectal, hepatocellular and ovarian cancer datasets. SpaceMACE retained the high precision of the original MACE framework while improving the spatial coherence of tumour-cell annotations. Together, these results demonstrate that SpaceMACE provides a scalable and platform-independent framework for tumour-cell annotation in spatial transcriptomics and supports the spatial investigation of tumour-specific molecular targets.

items.title: Cell-state conditioning predicts the expression response to an unseen stimulus but not stimulus-dependent genetic effects
items.blurb: Second-generation sequence models can be conditioned on a cell state supplied as a single-cell snapshot rather than selected from a fixed catalogue, but whether that conditioning carries an experimentally applied perturbation has not been tested. We conditioned such a model on interferon-{beta}-stimulated and unstimulated monocytes from a published experiment, using cells disjoint from those providing the measurement, and asked whether the predicted expression response tracks the measured one and whether the same conditioning identifies expression QTL specific to the stimulated state. Predicted and measured responses agree at Spearman {rho} = 0.616 across 119 genes (95% CI 0.486 to 0.716), and at 0.607 after all 119 target genes are deleted from the conditioning input; across fifteen conditions the model's response scales with how much each condition's biology genuinely overlaps the target response (slope 0.73, Pearson 0.92), and a near-neighbour monocyte subset receives 0.295 against a measured overlap of 0.336. For stimulation-specific genetic effects we find no reliable evidence: the pre-specified primary arm moves from p = 0.0019 to 0.443 once both conditions must carry a measurable predicted effect, and the separation localises to the resting-condition baseline. Neither model generation's catalogue contains a perturbed sample, 0 of 4,430 tracks and 0 of 2,799 conditions, although both carry activation-state labels, so the gap is experimental perturbation rather than cell state. Two incidental findings apply beyond this model: credible-set membership mislabels over half of putatively condition-specific loci, and gating a ratio statistic on its larger term manufactures signal.

items.title: High-throughput identification of changes in cellular localization for RNA-binding proteins during adenovirus infection reveals viral harnessing of nuclear speckles
items.blurb: Adenovirus (AdV) is a human DNA virus reliant on host RNA processing machinery. While research into AdV has yielded landmark discoveries in RNA biology, studies investigating the scope of AdV dependency on specific host RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are lacking. Here we performed optical pooled screening on a cell library where hundreds of RBPs are endogenously tagged. Pooled imaging followed by in situ barcode sequencing revealed a broad view of virus-induced host RBP relocalization patterns, including those recruited to viral replication compartments (VRCs). A targeted siRNA screen of relocalized RBPs demonstrated a requirement for the nuclear speckle (NS) core protein SON during virus infection. Depletion of SON resulted in reduced viral gene expression, impaired NS protein recruitment to early-stage VRCs, and impaired mobility of SRRM2 during infection. These findings suggest a crucial role of SON and NS functions in regulating viral gene expression and demonstrate the power of pooled tagging coupled to optical screening in investigating virus-host interactions.

items.title: Three-Dimensional Refractive Index Patterns Distinguish CD57-Defined Subsets of Human Memory T Cells
items.blurb: Distinguishing T-cell subsets is important for characterizing immune differentiation, but label-free classification is challenging because closely related subsets have overlapping biophysical properties. We combined holotomography with a three-dimensional convolutional neural network to classify primary human T cells from their refractive index (RI) tomograms. Fluorescence-activated cell sorting defined four reference populations: CD4+, naive CD8+, and CD57- and CD57+ memory CD8+ T cells. The FishNet-inspired classifier achieved 97.04% accuracy in a cell-level held-out test of 270 cells. Dedicated binary classifiers achieved 97.70% accuracy for naive versus CCR7- memory CD8+ cells and 94.44% for CD57- versus CD57+ memory CD8+ cells. Although the memory subsets overlapped in whole-cell descriptors, their volumetric RI patterns supported classification. These findings establish a basis for investigating intrinsic optical phenotypes associated with CD57-defined T-cell differentiation.

items.title: Integrated multi-omics reveals organ-specific jasmonate signaling in Arabidopsis under combined heat and phosphate starvation
items.blurb: Phosphate (Pi) limitation is a major constraint on plant productivity and is aggravated by heat stress. In nature, soil buffers air temperature, creating a vertical thermal gradient that shields roots from extreme heat; thus, heat and Pi starvation, although often co-occurring, are perceived mainly by different organs, shoots and roots respectively. How plants integrate these organ-specific stresses into a coordinated response remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated how Arabidopsis responds to combined Pi deficiency and elevated temperature, using a root-zone temperature gradient and an integrated analysis of ion accumulation, phytohormone levels and transcriptomic profiles in roots and shoots. The combined stress elicited a distinct response that cannot be explained by the addition of individual stress effects. Jasmonate levels changed in an organ-specific manner, with JA-Ile accumulating in roots and JA declining in shoots, and mutants with reduced (jar1-1) or constitutive (jazQ) JA signaling showed altered transcriptional, growth and leaf-temperature responses. These results identify jasmonic acid (JA) as a modulator of the balance between acclimation and growth under combined nutritional and thermal limitation, advancing our understanding of how plants cope with the multi-stress scenarios driven by climate change.

items.title: Role of Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) in muscle fatigue: significance for muscle myopathies
items.blurb: We report that Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) modulates skeletal muscle function. TLR2 ligands accelerated muscle fatigue development in isolated muscle fibers. Muscle fibers from TLR2 gene knock-out (TLR2-/-) mice were more fatigue resistant. This was not due to altered mitochondrial oxidative capacity or glycogen content. TLR2-/- muscle fibers had larger tetanic [Ca2+]i transients. Muscles from TLR2-/- mice had increased levels of Ca2+-binding proteins compared to WT muscles. Lastly, TLR2 was expressed in muscle fibers of control subjects and patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM), whereas high mobility group box protein (HMGB) 1, an endogenous activator of TLR2, was only detected in the cytoplasm of muscles from IIM patients. In conclusion, TLR2 signaling regulates force production in skeletal muscle. TLR2 and its endogenous ligand, HMGB1 likely contribute to the muscle weakness in IIM and, possibly, other muscle disorders. Therapies targeted to the TLR2 signaling pathway may counteract pathological muscle weakness.

items.title: Tissue-specific biotransformation shapes the toxicity of 6PPD-quinone in fish cell models
items.blurb: Acute mortality of salmonids exposed to urban runoff has been linked to 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q), a transformation product of the widely used tire antiozonant 6PPD. However, the cellular processes underlying 6PPD-Q toxicity remain poorly understood. Beyond the well-documented differences in species sensitivity, here we determined tissue-specific responses in rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) cell lines exposed to 6PPD-Q: brain-derived cells (RTBrain) were more sensitive than gill-derived cells (RTgill-W1). To unravel the cellular mechanisms underlying such differential responses, we combined time-resolved 6PPD-Q cellular depletion kinetics, targeted biotransformation product (BTP) profiling, transporter inhibition experiments, and cytotoxicity assessments. Both cell models biotransformed 6PPD-Q, but RTBrain displayed a 6.6-fold higher cellular clearance rate than RTgill-W1. Chemical profiling identified four BTPs, including para-aryl-OH-6PPD-Q, which was selectively toxic to RTBrain but not RTgill-W1 cells. These findings reveal tissue-specific toxicokinetics as potential determinants of differential 6PPD-Q toxicity even within the same species. More broadly, this integrated approach highlights the importance of considering biotransformation and the production of biologically active transformation products when assessing susceptibility to emerging contaminants.

items.title: Measuring Phylogenetic Information Content Based on Clade Support
items.blurb: Phylogenetic information content is often understood as the degree to which data lend support to hypotheses about the monophyly of clades. This is most commonly expressed in terms of clade support, typically estimated by resampling techniques such as the bootstrap and the jackknife. Here, I discuss how to summarize this aspect of data quality. I show that raw bootstrap or jackknife proportions are unsuitable for this purpose and instead suggest a logarithmic transformation, which can be interpreted as translating the clade support values to the number of characters expected to give the same resampling proportion in parsimony analysis of a homoplasy-free data matrix. The distribution of the number of these "supporting characters" and descriptive statistics derived from this distribution, such as the mean (Mean Character Support, or MCS) and its standard deviation, provide powerful summaries of the quality of the underlying data set. I demonstrate for both empirical and simulated data sets that MCS accurately reflects information content, and that some popular alternative measures of data quality (the ensemble consistency index, the ensemble retention index, data decisiveness and the total support index) do not. Unlike most other measures of data quality, MCS can be applied to trees resulting from a range of alternative phylogenetic methods, including parsimony, distance and maximum likelihood approaches.

items.title: Policy-Enforced Genomic Repositories and Institutional Data Governance for African Pathogen Surveillance with UbuntuBio
items.blurb: Research centers curating pathogen sequence cohorts often operate under constrained bandwidth, multi-institutional data-sharing agreements, and strict biosafety requirements. Global public archives keep released sequences permanently open, external viral portals enforce terms outside local institutional custody, and standard Git Large File Storage (LFS) duplicates identical binaries across repositories without validating taxonomy or geography. We present UbuntuBio (v1.0.0), a Git-native, policy-enforced genomic repository platform deployed at https://ubuntubio.org and developed at the West African Centre for Cell Biology of Infectious Pathogens (WACCBIP), University of Ghana. UbuntuBio integrates four mechanisms under a single storage root: (1) bare Git repositories storing dataset cards, sample sheets, and approximately 130-byte LFS pointers backed by prefix-sharded SHA-256 content-addressed storage (CAS) with visibility-scoped wire deduplication; (2) a four-phase commit pipeline recoverable via cross-plane reconciliation that enforces 55 African Union country codes against offline Natural Earth polygons, core MIxS-derived fields, Taxon 9606 rejection, and server-keyed targeted human-marker screening identically across HTTP commits and Git pre-receive hooks; (3) institutional custody controls combining Data Use Agreements (DUAs), revocable 900-second RS256 capability tokens, key rotation, tamper-evident hash-chained logs, and externally anchorable RS256 audit checkpoints; and (4) an embedded SQLite WAL and FTS5 catalog filtered by access tier. In single-node evaluation, UbuntuBio classified 18/18 policy boundary fixtures consistently across Python, Git, and HTTP paths; showed 0/265,157 false cross-matches on 21/22 RefSeq pathogen sequences (while cross-matching Candida albicans 18S rDNA at 0.113% and Chlorocebus sabaeus Alu repeats in ENA stool reads, confirming targeted marker detection rather than verified human DNA decontamination); matched conditional uniform (n = 2,000; 200-seed 0.01% convergence 19.0% vs. 18.13% expected) and interior (n = 1,000) detection theory while detecting all spike-ins at [≥] 0.5% (30/30); halved two-repository disk usage on 613.83 MiB Nigerian E. coli runs; passed 27/27 structured-filter correctness checks over 10,000 biosamples and reached graded NDCG@10 = 0.920 on independent free-text BM25 queries with zero private leaks; and recovered cleanly across seven injected phase-transition faults.

items.title: KORUS: probabilistic ancestry inference beyond variant calls
items.blurb: Ancestry inference typically relies on variant calling and predefined population labels. We present KORUS, a probabilistic framework that infers ancestry from sequencing-derived k-mer representations constructed using ancestry-informative reference variants and encoded in Bloom filters, without requiring explicit variant calls for query genomes. KORUS separates genomic feature representation from ancestry decoding, enabling supervised classification, fractional ancestry inference, and unsupervised population structure discovery within a unified framework. Reference models were constructed from 643 genomes from the 1000 Genomes Project and the Simons Genome Diversity Project. Evaluation on an independent cohort of 22 whole-genome sequencing samples, with comparisons to ntRoot, SNVstory, and ADMIXTURE, showed recovery of continental-scale population structure, with supervised classification accuracy of 72.7-81.8% and ancestry-fraction concordance of R2 = 0.844-0.993 relative to ADMIXTURE and R2 = 0.665-0.983 relative to ntRoot. Ancestry estimates were consistent across alternative k-mer representations. Analyses of ancient human and archaic hominin genomes demonstrated that probabilistic projections quantify affinity to the learned feature space rather than necessarily indicating modern continental ancestry. KORUS provides a unified approach to ancestry inference directly from sequencing-derived representations and is freely available under the GPLv3 license at https://github.com/BirolLab/korus.

items.title: The pangenome of the Arctic picoeukaryote Micromonas polaris resolves cryptic ecotypes and identifies a polar-specific gene repertoire
items.blurb: Micromonas polaris is the dominant picoeukaryote of the Arctic Ocean, where it sustains primary production across habitats from sea ice to open water to the subsurface chlorophyll maximum. How a single species maintains this ecological breadth has remained unclear. Standard phylogenetic markers such as 18S rRNA are nearly invariant within M. polaris and conceal any internal genomic heterogeneity the species may possess. Here we present a pangenome of 14 M. polaris strains spanning the Arctic basin, integrated with Tara Oceans metagenomes, that resolves the species into two diverged ecotypes invisible to 18S rRNA but recovered consistently by prp8, genome-wide SNPs, ANI, and orthogroup-based phylogenies. The two ecotypes coexist sympatrically, with one lineage consistently enriched deeper in the water column across the basin. M. polaris carries 990 polar-specific hierarchical orthogroups absent from temperate Micromonas, organised around one-carbon metabolism, endocytosis, transmembrane transport, and photo-oxidative stress response. Several components show phylogenetic signatures of horizontal acquisition from co-occurring marine taxa. Atlantification is bringing temperate Micromonas into Arctic margins seasonally, but the polar night likely limits their year-round persistence. M. polaris and its polar-specific toolkit appear positioned to persist through the dark season, suggesting Arctic margins will undergo seasonal turnover rather than stable replacement.

items.title: Vertical transmission and community turnover in seed-borne microbiomes: lessons from an aMAIZEing model system
items.blurb: The seed microbiome represents a specialized ecological niche, governed by assembly processes that are only partially coupled to the surrounding soil community. While environmental recruitment and vertical transmission from the maternal plant are both recognized sources of seed-associated microorganisms, the mechanisms that determine their relative contributions and whether these contributions shift across generations remain poorly understood. Here, we used long-read metagenomic sequencing to track seed-borne bacterial community dynamics across a founding seed pool and two subsequent generations in two divergent maize (Zea mays L.) varieties exposed to contrasting organic and mineral fertilisation regimes. We recovered 112 medium- or high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes and combined MAG-level taxonomic and functional analyses with genus-level community profiling to characterize persistence and turnover dynamics within the seed microbiome. While soil taxonomic diversity was high, seed-associated communities showed a near-complete compositional disconnect from soil-dominant assemblages taxa, with a persistent Firmicutes core maintained across generations, consistent with vertical transmission. Priority effects remain a possible explanation for these patterns but were not directly tested. Genus-level source attribution suggested greater environmental recruitment under organic fertilization, with more diverse soil communities and a stronger contribution from the preceding seed generation under mineral fertilization. Seed-associated MAGs also carried genes associated with plant growth-promoting potential, although these detections could not be consistently linked to specific transmission routes. In contrast, maize genotype had no detectable effect on seed microbiome composition. Intergenerational persistence and environmental recruitment jointly shape seed-derived communities under contrasting fertilization regimes. Their relative contributions remain inferred from taxonomic overlap, and the effects of microbial source-pool diversity cannot be separated from the accompanying differences in soil chemistry in this design.

items.title: Maternal obesity disrupts glucose oxidation and mitochondrial fission in the myometrium at term gestation
items.blurb: Women with obesity experience delayed spontaneous labor onset, slow labor progression, and elevated risk of labor dystocia, but the underlying mechanisms are poorly understood. We previously established a mouse model of diet-induced obesity that exhibits decreased uterine contractility, labor dystocia, and elevated fatty acids in the myometrium. Here, we used this model to determine how maternal obesity affects energy production and mitochondrial homeostasis in the myometrium at term. Myometrium tissue and myometrial smooth muscle cells from diet-induced obese mice at term showed decreased pyruvate utilization, inhibition of glucose oxidation, and disruption of mitochondrial fission and mitophagy. Treatment with medium-chain fatty acids in both murine and human primary myometrial cells resulted in significant decreases in abundance of mitochondrial fission proteins. Finally, mitochondrial spare capacity in human myometrial cells decreased with body mass index of the patient providing the cells. Taken together, these findings indicate that fatty acid accumulation dysregulates energy metabolism and mitochondrial homeostasis in the myometrium and may contribute to dysfunctional labor in women with obesity.

items.title: GCase deficiency impairs uptake of α-synuclein-loaded ectosome by astrocytes
items.blurb: Parkinson's disease (PD) involves the prion-like propagation of -synuclein. One mechanism for the spread of -synuclein between neurons in PD is ectosomes. But PD is a multicellular disorder in which astrocytes also play a critical role. How astrocytes take up ectosomes and whether this is affected in PD is unclear. Here we show that GCase-deficiency, as occurs in PD, impairs astrocytic uptake of neuron-derived ectosomes containing -synuclein. The defect in ectosome uptake by astrocytes is driven by compromised macropinocytosis and can be rescued by reducing glucosylceramides or restoring lysosomal function. These findings identify sphingolipid metabolism as a key regulator of ectosome uptake by primary and iPSC-derived astrocytes. They also support a shift from the uptake and clearance of -synuclein by astrocytes in health, towards the transmission of -synuclein pathology towards neurons in PD.

items.title: Quiescent Cells Exhibit a Senescence-Like Secretory Phenotype
items.blurb: Cellular quiescence is traditionally considered a reversible state of cell cycle arrest, distinct from senescence, which is associated with a characteristic senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). However, whether quiescent cells exhibit a comparable secretory program remains poorly understood. Here, we identify and characterize a Quiescence-Associated Secretory Phenotype (QASP) by integrating single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing datasets from human fibroblasts and preadipocytes. We find that quiescent cells exhibit increased expression of genes encoding inflammatory mediators and extracellular matrix-associated proteins, with substantial overlap between the QASP and SASP. This transcriptional program is highly heterogeneous, varying across cell types, quiescence induction methods, and environmental oxygen levels. In particular, contact inhibition induces a stronger inflammatory signature than serum withdrawal in several cellular contexts. Multiplexed cytokine profiling demonstrated active secretion of inflammatory mediators, including IL-1{beta}, IL-6, IL-15, and CCL2, in quiescent fibroblasts, with secretion levels varying by induction method and generally higher following contact inhibition than serum withdrawal. Analysis of single-cell transcriptomic data from human lung tissue further reveals increased QASP-associated gene expression in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), particularly in myofibroblasts, linking this phenotype to inflammatory signaling and extracellular matrix remodeling. Together, these findings identify the QASP as a context-dependent secretory program that shares features with the SASP and may contribute to inflammatory signaling and extracellular matrix remodeling in both physiological and pathological conditions.

items.title: Three novel deep-branching orphan protist lineages from the marine rare biosphere
items.blurb: Metabarcoding has transformed our view of marine protist communities, yet many sequences in environmental surveys are not assigned confident taxonomic identity. These taxonomically ambiguous sequences may include lineages that are not within any known eukaryotic supergroup, which we refer to here as orphan lineages. These orphan lineages matter beyond taxonomy-based community analyses, because they can help us understand early eukaryotic evolution. Here we used phylogenetic inferences and sequence similarity networks (SSNs) of long-read metabarcoding data of the ribosomal operon (18S-28S rDNA) to identify three novel phylum-level orphan lineages. We designate these lineages Deep Orphan Lineages 1-3 (DEEPOLs) and show that they are exclusively marine and part of the rare biosphere, yet ecologically distinct: DEEPOL1 is a cosmopolitan generalist, DEEPOL2 a conditionally rare lineage capable of local polar blooms, and DEEPOL3 a non-polar lineage with a tendency toward the dark ocean. For DEEPOL2, lineage-specific digital PCR (dPCR) combined with catalyzed reporter deposition fluorescence in situ hybridization (CARD-FISH) provides the first in situ visualization of these cells, revealing small, flagellated, and morphologically inconspicuous protists. Together, our results show that substantial diversity remains hidden among rare lineages, and that long-read sequencing combined with targeted molecular and microscopy approaches offers a first step toward linking orphan sequences to organisms and their evolution and ecological roles.

items.title: Single-cell genomics reveals genomic and functional differentiation between freshwater and saline Achromatium populations.
items.blurb: Giant sulfur bacteria of the genus Achromatium reportedly contain extensive genomic diversity within individual cells. Most genomic data (35 assemblies) come from freshwater populations obtained from Lake Stechlin, Germany, alongside four single-cell genomes from a salt marsh and saline mineral springs. Here, we characterize marine Achromatium from mangrove sediments in Guadeloupe and compare them with freshwater and saline references. Microscopy, elemental mapping, and Raman spectroscopy revealed calcium-rich inclusions, and intracellular elemental sulfur as previously described for this genus. Scanning electron microscopy revealed two cell-size morphotypes. We generated eleven single-cell, four mixed-cell, and two metagenomic binned assemblies from Guadeloupe mangrove. Divergent copies of conserved marker genes revealed extensive intracellular genomic diversity in individual cells of both morphotypes. Multigene phylogenies provided separation between freshwater references and most genomes from saline environments, including the Guadeloupe population. Gene presence-absence analyses further revealed differences in functional potential between Guadeloupe and Stechlin cells across five functional annotation categories including PFAM, KEGG Orthologs, and CAZymes. Differences in genes associated with osmotic regulation, ion transport, carbohydrate degradation, and secretion systems suggest variation in functional potential related to environmental adaptation, interactions and resource utilization. No significant differences in functional potential between Guadeloupe morphotypes were found. Together, these marine genomes reveal genomic and functional differentiation from freshwater populations and suggest that intracellular diversity does not erase freshwater/saline population boundaries.

items.title: Biphasic glycocalyx remodelling balances immune cell recruitment and tissue damage during influenza infection
items.blurb: The endothelial glycocalyx is a glycan-rich barrier lining blood vessels that regulates immune cell recruitment, whose role in viral infection is unknown. Using a murine influenza model, we reveal that the lung endothelial glycocalyx undergoes coordinated biphasic remodelling: early shedding followed by substantial accumulation during peak immune activation. Genetic deletion of heparanase, the enzyme driving early glycocalyx shedding, reduced immune cell lung infiltration and improved host recovery. Conversely, using a new endothelial-specific glycocalyx depletion mouse model, we demonstrate that this glycocalyx accumulation actively limits immune cell recruitment and prevents excessive tissue damage. Together, these findings reveal that coordinated endothelial and immune cell glycocalyx remodelling is an active and previously unrecognised regulator of the balance between antiviral immune cell recruitment and tissue protection.

items.title: Gene expression in the hypothalamus of gonad-sex chromosome divergent embryonic chickens
items.blurb: Sexual differentiation of the brain of birds is shaped by gonadal steroid hormones and also by cell-autonomous mechanisms resulting from limited sex chromosome dosage compensation. In this study, we compare gene expression in the hypothalamus of gonad-sex chromosome divergent embryonic chickens treated with the aromatase inhibitor fadrozole to their control counterparts. Consistent with a lack of dosage compensation, we find a robust effect of sex chromosomes on hypothalamic gene expression, and a large portion of differentially expressed genes were on the Z and W sex chromosomes. Despite the presence of developing testes and markedly reduced estrogen concentrations in fadrozole-treated chromosomal female (ZW) birds, we find modest effects of gonadal hormones on gene expression in the brain. Weighted gene coexpression network analysis revealed that the most prominent effects were attributable to interactions between chromosomal sex and treatment. Our results highlight that chromosomal sex and steroid hormones together shape the sexual differentiation of the embryonic avian brain, challenging the primacy of the organizational effects of sex steroids on the brain during development.

items.title: A radial glial regulatory program bridges progenitor maintenance and neuronal identity
items.blurb: The cerebral cortex acquires its neuronal diversity through successive waves of neurogenesis. How molecular differences among early progenitors relate to their neuronal output remains unclear. Here, we identify a molecular program in early SOX9-high radial glia (S9RGs) that links progenitor maintenance with the regulation of genes associated with neuronal identity. Combining transcriptional and chromatin profiling with in vivo perturbations, we identify a program involving extracellular signaling, cell-cycle regulation, progenitor maintenance, and neurogenesis. We show that SOX9 regulates part of this program, including receptors that contribute to progenitor maintenance, while Notch acts upstream of Sox9 and reproduces several transcriptional and chromatin features of S9RGs. S9RGs express selected later-stage radial glial features and show distinct chromatin accessibility patterns at genes involved in progenitor maintenance, neurogenesis, and neuronal identity. Notch activation reproduces part of these changes, including differences at genes associated with lower- and upper-layer neuronal specification. Interestingly, S9RGs, which preferentially generate upper-layer neurons, share molecular features with the highly proliferative RG population in ferrets and with human outer RGs (oRGs) from cortical organoids, despite their different positions within the developing cortex. Together, our findings suggest that molecular differences among early radial glia could influence both how long they remain as progenitors and the neuronal identities they subsequently generate.

items.title: Genetic, neural and early-environmental architecture of resilience
items.blurb: Resilience is shaped by factors ranging from the genome through early-life experience to the brain, yet its biological basis in humans remains unclear because studies have rarely integrated these levels and have been confined to small samples. Using the Brief Resilience Scale (BRS) and multimodal data from tens of thousands of UK Biobank (UKB) participants, with replication in Generation Scotland (GS), we found that resting-state functional connectivity, particularly within the flexibility and valuation networks, is a robust neural correlate of resilience. Resilience also showed a generalizable genetic basis: a polygenic score (PGS) derived from a UKB genome-wide association study predicted BRS in GS. Genes and childhood experiences converged on the flexibility network through distinct routes: the polygenic association with resilience was partly explained by central executive-salience integration, whereas childhood experiences were associated with default-mode-centered integration. By separating genetically anchored from experience-sensitive routes, these findings point to network targets that interventions could tailor to the sources of an individual's vulnerability.

items.title: Neural reactivation of past events tracks narrative understanding as it unfolds
items.blurb: Understanding of episodic experience is not achieved at a single moment: it is a constructive process in which each new event is interpreted in light of relevant past events and prior knowledge. Yet this process is rarely measured as it unfolds, leaving unclear how the brain integrates past events to construct an evolving understanding of the present. We hypothesized that neural reactivation of past events at narrative event boundaries reflects not merely what people experience, but how they interpret their experience. We developed a behavioural paradigm that tracks, as a narrative unfolds, which past events people consider relevant for understanding each new event. By manipulating prior knowledge of the narrative's final plot twist, we examined the process by which the same experience yields different understanding. Across independent behavioural and fMRI cohorts, we found that prior knowledge similarly altered the variability and intersubject similarity of inferred relations between events and their neural reactivation at narrative event boundaries in the Default Mode Network. Moreover, stronger neural reactivation was associated with greater inferred relevance between events, and event pairs showing different behavioural relations across groups also showed corresponding differences in reactivation. These findings suggest that neural reactivation of past events at event boundaries reflects an unfolding inferential process that transforms shared experience into subjective understanding.

items.title: A temporal atlas of TDP-43 interactions reveals persistent network remodelling beyond stress granule clearance
items.blurb: Cytoplasmic aggregation of the nuclear protein TDP-43 is associated with several neurodegenerative disorders and may be promoted by cellular stress. However, the dynamics of TDP-43 protein-protein interactions during stress and recovery remain poorly understood. Here, we combined APEX2 proximity labelling with quantitative mass spectrometry to generate a temporal atlas of wild-type TDP-43 and pathology-mimicking TDP-43dNLS and TDP-43CTF variants. Interactomes were profiled across steady state, oxidative stress, and recovery. We reveal extensive state- and variant-dependent remodelling of TDP-43 interaction networks, uncovering distinct temporal interaction patterns throughout the stress response and recovery. Notably, distinct TDP-43 interaction signatures persisted after stress granule clearance, suggesting a molecular memory of stress. Together, our study establishes a comprehensive temporal resource for investigating TDP-43 interaction dynamics and provides a framework for understanding how stress-induced network alterations may contribute to TDP-43 proteinopathies.

items.blurb:
Translated into English in thrilling style, these interlinked stories of ambushes and vendettas vividly evoke the bitter conflict of the 1919-22 Greco-Turkish war

Nine interconnected tales about the violence of the 1919-22 Greco-Turkish war, and the struggles of its broken soldiers to reassimilate into civilian life, Gjak is something of a sensation. Originally written in Greek and Arvanitic, a dialect spoken by a Greco-Albanian ethnic group, and featuring characters from an unspecified Arvanite village, it was a hit in Greece in 2014 and comes to the UK in an agile translation by Siân Valvis. In her fascinating introductory note, Valvis writes of her attempt to capture the “unruly, galloping force” of Dimosthenis Papamarkos’s prose. She succeeds in thrilling style.

Delivered in a demotic, gossipy voice, these are rough-hewn stories of ambushes and vendettas, of brothers in arms being “closer than kin” and of lingering, sour regret. One of the translations of the eponymous Arvanitic word “gjak” is “blood” and indeed, graphic bloodiness is inescapable. Narrators don’t shy away from descriptions of how “shrapnel sliced [them] up like a fillet – eyes, teeth, ripped off half a jaw”.

items.title: The Man Who Broke Reality by Philip Ball review – the inspirational genius of Niels Bohr
items.blurb:
Scientific discoveries are effortlessly explained in this portrait of a man whose research was driven by passion

Niels Bohr shares with Albert Einstein pride of place in the pantheon of 20th-century science. The two had much in common. They were not expert mathematicians; they prized physical intuition over mere competence; and they did not shy away from the moral and political implications of their work.

But Bohr differed from Einstein in one crucial respect: his extraordinary personality. In his gripping biography Philip Ball ensures we feel the intense pull of Bohr’s genius. Today he would probably be considered neurodivergent; he possessed a passion for physics that cast a spell on all who knew him. Solving problems is the raison d’etre of any scientist, but Bohr went far beyond that: having inaugurated quantum mechanics with his model of the atom in 1913, he simply would not give up until the rest of it was understood.

items.title: The Guardian view on climate debt: a vicious cycle the world must break at Cop31 | Editorial
items.blurb:
Poor countries are paying creditors instead of preparing for climate disasters. The international financial system must stop deepening their vulnerability

The catastrophe that struck Nepal’s Himalayas in August began with a collapsing glacier. An avalanche of ice and rock unleashed deadly floods, sweeping away villages, bridges and roads, and leaving thousands dead or missing. It illustrated the dangers posed by global heating to the Himalayas’ increasingly unstable glaciers. Nepal lost a tenth of its electricity generation. Reconstruction will cost about $5bn. Yet the Loss and Damage Fund, hailed as a historic breakthrough at the 2022 UN climate summit, has earmarked just $20m for Nepal – less than 5% of the $482m that Kathmandu must pay its external public creditors this year.

“The scale of resources needs to increase,” Nepal’s delegation to this year’s UN climate conference drily observed. They are not the only ones agitating for change at Cop31. In its September report, Debt Fuels the Climate Crisis, ActionAid noted that the global south’s external borrowing is 100 times more than the climate finance it received. Poor nations end up trapped in debt dependency because they export cheap raw materials, but import expensive food, fuel and manufactured goods, invariably priced in dollars. The charity warned that climate-vulnerable countries are now expected to fund decarbonisation while servicing dollar loans that often pressure them to export fossil fuels rather than invest in green industrialisation.

The so-called sorry state of the vegan restaurant scene has been widely reported on (not least by me). But after working with the food magazine Vittles on its inaugural London vegan guide, I have begun to challenge the “death of vegan dining” narrative that I had found myself perpetuating. And yes, a depressing number of my choices for the Vegan 99 closed while I was writing it; most recently, an omnivorous Malaysian restaurant with a walloping double-tofu laksa, which shut 24 hours before publication. But the process encouraged me to take a different viewpoint, instead focusing on the spots that had survived and the story they told.

items.title: Afghanistan: Humanitarian Update, October 2026
items.blurb:
Country: Afghanistan
Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

Please refer to the attached file.

Funding shortfalls threaten winter response in Afghanistan

As temperatures begin to fall across Afghanistan, humanitarian partners are ramping up winter preparedness amid significant funding constraints. Aid organizations are pre-positioning supplies to enable them to deliver assistance before access to remote communities becomes more challenging. With needs expected to remain high, the humanitarian response enters the winter season facing a substantial funding gap, raising concerns about being able to reach all those in need and forcing difficult choices about how the limited resources are prioritized.

The 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan requires US$1.71 billion to provide life-saving assistance and protection across Afghanistan. However, as of October, only $550 million has been received through the Plan, meaning 68 per cent of funding requirements remain unmet. This shortfall threatens efforts to support vulnerable communities during one of the most challenging seasons of the year.

Winter often brings heightened humanitarian risks across Afghanistan. In many provinces, heavy snowfall and freezing temperatures can isolate communities, disrupt transportation routes and limit access to markets, health facilities and other essential services. For households already struggling with poverty, food insecurity, climate-related shocks and limited livelihood opportunities, the cold season brings additional pressure as families seek to secure food, heating fuel, warm clothing and adequate shelter.

As winter approaches, many vulnerable families are expected to face increasing pressure as food prices, heating costs and other seasonal expenses rise while livelihood opportunities decline. Yet several critical sectors remain significantly underfunded.

Food Security and Agriculture, the largest sector in the humanitarian response, has received only 18.2 per cent of its funding requirements despite continued concerns over food insecurity across the country. As winter conditions reduce income-generating opportunities and increase household expenditure on food, fuel and other essentials, many families are likely to face greater difficulties in meeting their basic needs.

Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items cluster, which provides vulnerable households with shelter support, essential household items and winter assistance, has received only 15.1 per cent of the funding required. Water, Sanitation and Hygiene programmes are similarly underfunded, with just 16.6 per cent of requirements met, while Nutrition activities have received 16.3 per cent. Health is funded at 45.4 per cent, leaving significant gaps in essential services, particularly as winter conditions increase the risk of respiratory infections and other seasonal illnesses.

Together, these funding shortfalls risk limiting access to food, shelter, health care, safe water and nutrition support during one of the most challenging periods of the year, potentially leaving vulnerable households with fewer options to cope.

items.title: oPt: Gaza's Education Crisis: A System-Wide Collapse Threatening an Entire Generation
items.blurb:
Country: occupied Palestinian territory
Source: American Near East Refugee Aid

Please refer to the attached file.

AN ENTIRE GENERATION OUT OF SCHOOL

The war that began on October 7, 2023 did not just interrupt schooling in Gaza, it dismantled the education system that more than 750,000 learners, from preschool through university, once relied on.1 Nearly all schools have been damaged or destroyed, and for over two years, students of all ages have had little to no access to formal learning.

A child who was seven when this began is now nine or ten, and has spent a third of the life that they can remember waiting for school to resume.

This report is based on Anera's Gaza Education Sector Needs Assessment, which draws on interviews and focus group discussions with teachers, parents, students, education officials and community members across Gaza, alongside secondary data from UNRWA, UNICEF, the Education Cluster, the Palestine Central Bureau of Statistics and other humanitarian and education partners.

What emerges is a story of systemic collapse in education, one that has stripped away not just classrooms, but the routines, relationships and sense of future that schooling once provided. The war's psychological toll is equally profound. Children have endured repeated familial displacement, loss and violence, while teachers are coping with their own trauma even as they try to support students.

Yet, despite overwhelming challenges, Gaza's communities continue to demonstrate remarkable tenacity. Parents, volunteers and educators have created informal classrooms and learning activities wherever possible, underscoring the determination to keep young people learning and the urgent need for sustained international support. Children cannot recover academically without first having stability, routine and protection. Restoring education in Gaza should therefore begin with three essentials: safe places to learn, teachers who are supported and able to teach, and basic classroom resources.

This report tells the story of what has been lost and lays out what must happen next.

items.title: 2025 Annual Report: Libya: Division Entrenches Violations and Undermines Accountability [EN/AR]
items.blurb:
Country: Libya
Source: Libya Crimes Watch

Please refer to the attached files.

Libya Crimes Watch Issues Its 2025 Annual Report

London, 8 April 2026 — Libya Crimes Watch (LCW) has published its 2025 Annual Report, entitled “LIBYA: DIVISION ENTRENCHES VIOLATIONS AND UNDERMINES ACCOUNTABILITY“, documenting the continued and escalating grave human rights violations and international crimes occurring across the country, against a backdrop of the absence of effective accountability pathways and the persistence of impunity.

The report records 859 grave violations documented during 2025, compared to 589 during 2024, reflecting a significant increase in the rate of violations. It draws primarily on 93 documentation files and direct testimonies from victims, survivors, and witnesses collected by LCW’s field team in accordance with LCW’s established documentation methodology, which is aligned with international protocols for the documentation of human rights violations. These violations affected 617 civilians and occurred across at least 29 major areas and cities in eastern, southern, and western Libya, including remote and hard-to-reach areas.

The report provides a legal analysis of the documented violations in light of IHRL and IHL, drawing on indicators that measure the gravity, patterns, and scale of violations, and concludes that certain of these violations may constitute international crimes by virtue of their systematic nature and scale.

The Annual Report highlights the continuation of serious patterns of violations, including arbitrary detention, enforced disappearance, torture and ill-treatment, extrajudicial killing, and the denial of basic fair trial guarantees, alongside trafficking in persons, forced labour, and sexual violence. It further documents the repeated targeting of human rights defenders, activists, journalists, and dissidents for exercising their fundamental rights, including freedom of expression and participation in public life.

The report addresses violations committed against migrants, asylum seekers, and refugees, as well as vulnerable and marginalised groups, including women, children, and religious, ethnic, and gender minorities, and highlights the various contexts in which these violations occurred, including casualties resulting from military operations, encompassing armed clashes and the explosion of ERW.

The 2025 Annual Report identifies the responsibility of the authorities in eastern and western Libya for these violations, as well as that of prominent commanders and officials, whether for their commission by affiliated or supporting security apparatuses and armed groups, or for their failure to fulfil legal obligations to prevent violations, protect civilians, investigate incidents, and ensure the accountability of perpetrators. The report further highlights the continued inability of the national justice system to conduct independent and effective investigations, and the persistent weakness of cooperation with international justice mechanisms, including the ICC.

Commenting on the report, Ali Omar, Executive Director of Libya Crimes Watch, stated:

“Every year we find ourselves confronted with the same patterns of violations recurring, whilst victims and their families continue to await justice. This reality reflects an ongoing failure by the Libyan authorities to halt violations and hold those responsible to account, and underscores the urgent need for serious action to bring an end to impunity.”

In its recommendations, LCW affirms the urgent need to take concrete steps to end grave violations and international crimes, ensure the accountability of those responsible, and end impunity, including through full cooperation with the ICC. It calls upon the authorities in eastern and western Libya to honour their legal obligations, guarantee the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms, and cease the targeting of civilians on account of their opinions or activities. It further urges the international community to support justice and accountability pathways and to cease any direct or indirect support to parties implicated in violations.

items.title: At least 64 children killed and 64 injured in Yemen as intensified hostilities approach three-month mark
items.blurb:
Country: Yemen
Source: UN Children's Fund

NEW YORK, 18 November 2026 – At least 64 children have been killed and 64 injured in Yemen since hostilities escalated on 3 September. The number of casualties is likely to increase as renewed fighting continues around densely populated areas, particularly in Taiz and Lahj.

“The rising number of children killed and injured in Yemen is devastating. It must stop,” said UNICEF Executive Director, Catherine Russell. “Behind every number is a child whose life has been cut short or changed forever.”

Basic services and infrastructure children depend on are also being directly impacted. At least seven schools and 28 health facilities, including five supported by UNICEF, have been damaged since the escalation began. On 2 November, an attack on the UNICEF-supported Al-Suqyah Health Centre in Lahj, which serves around 1,700 people, was reported to have killed five people, including three health workers.

At the same time, displacement is accelerating. More than 330,000 people, including an estimated 174,000 children, have been displaced since the beginning of the renewed military escalations. Many displaced families are sheltering in unfinished or damaged buildings and struggling to access food, safe water, and health care.

The situation in Taiz City is particularly alarming. With the main road from Aden closed and alternative routes insecure, more than 800,000 people have reportedly been cut off from humanitarian assistance as of late October. Water production has fallen by nearly 50 per cent, food and fuel prices have more than doubled, and shortages of medicines, fuel, medical oxygen and electricity are threatening emergency, maternal, and newborn care.

Across escalation-impacted areas, over 1,160 schools have closed or suspended learning, affecting more than half a million students. Meanwhile, around one in three children recently screened by UNICEF mobile health teams were found to be acutely malnourished. Overcrowded displacement sites, too few latrines, and limited access to safe water are also increasing the risk of disease.

UNICEF is expanding its emergency response to reach up to 350,000 people, redeploying health and nutrition mobile teams to displacement sites and affected communities in Aden, Lahj, Abyan, Marib and Taiz, scaling up emergency water and sanitation support, and providing psychosocial care and case management for children, including those who are unaccompanied or separated from their families.

“Yemen’s children have suffered so much. We urgently need safe and unimpeded humanitarian access,” said Russell. “All parties must comply with their obligations under international law. Children must be protected, including their access to essential services such as healthcare, education, safe water, and food.”

The Centre for Competence on Humanitarian Negotiation (CCHN) commissioned the Humanitarian Policy Group at ODI Global to conduct research on community-led negotiations, particularly the processes that community negotiators undertake to engage with authorities and armed actors for
humanitarian access and protection.

Specifically, the study seeks to answer the following research questions:

  • What triggers the decision to engage in direct negotiations?
  • How do community negotiators prepare for such engagements?
  • What is the process taken in negotiations?
  • What are their risk-mitigation strategies?
  • What are the tactics and strategies used in the negotiation process?
  • What factors influence the outcome of negotiations?
  • What follow-up actions take place once an agreement is reached?
  • What type of support do community negotiators most need?

The findings presented in this report identified that community negotiation practices are often instinctual, unstructured, and rarely documented. Stemming from 13 countries across diverse contexts, the results strongly suggest that community negotiators prepare strategically for dialogue, similarly to what is set out in the Naivasha Grid. As noted, the greater the international support, the more aligned the community negotiations become with international humanitarian practices. However, the process varies according to the context and is generally more organic than international negotiation practices.

items.blurb:
Countries: Chad, Sudan

Please refer to the attached file.

Réponse d’urgence à l’Est

L’afflux continu de réfugiés soudanais en quête de sécurité au Tchad accentue la pression sur les capacités d’accueil, particulièrement à Tiné, où le centre de transit accueille désormais plus de 9 000 réfugiés, soit neuf fois sa capacité initiale. Entre le 1er et le 15 novembre 2026, 5 411 nouveaux réfugiés soudanais ont été enregistrés dans les provinces du Ouaddaï, du Wadi Fira et de l’Ennedi Est, portant à plus de 989, 827 le nombre total de nouveaux arrivants accueillis au Tchad depuis le début du conflit au Soudan en avril 2023. Ces nouvelles arrivées sont principalement liées à la persistance des violences et de l’insécurité au Darfour, ainsi qu’aux attaques contre les infrastructures civiles. Conformément à sa tradition d’asile et au principe de non-refoulement, le Gouvernement tchadien a continué de garantir l’accès au territoire aux personnes fuyant le conflit au Soudan et à la protection internationale. Le HCR et ses partenaires ont poursuivi les activités d’enregistrement, de suivi de protection, de relocalisation et d’assistance vitale, avec une attention particulière portée aux personnes les plus vulnérables. Bien que le rythme des arrivées reste inférieur aux pics précédemment observés, notamment en septembre, la poursuite des mouvements transfrontaliers continue d’exercer une pression importante sur les capacités d’accueil, les services de protection et, plus largement, la réponse humanitaire dans l’est du Tchad. La relocalisation des réfugiés soudanais vers des sites plus sûrs se poursuit. Entre le 1er et le 15 novembre, le HCR et la CNARR ont relocalisé 2 170 réfugiés soudanais depuis la zone frontalière d’Adré vers Metché, dans le Ouaddaï, leur permettant ainsi d’accéder à de meilleures conditions de protection et aux services essentiels. Au 15 novembre 2026, 154 370 réfugiés restaient en attente de relocalisation dans les zones frontalières, notamment à Adré et à Tiné. La poursuite des opérations de relocalisation demeure essentielle pour réduire la pression sur des capacités d’accueil fortement sollicitées, offrir aux réfugiés des conditions plus sûres et améliorer leur accès à la protection et à l’assistance humanitaire. Mise en œuvre progressive de l’Approche basée sur la vulnérabilité et les capacités dans les sites de réfugiés de l’Est du Tchad. Entre le 26 et le 31 octobre 2026, le HCR et ses partenaires ont poursuivi la mise en œuvre de l’Approche basée sur la vulnérabilité et les capacités (ABVC) dans les sites accueillant des réfugiés dans l’est du Tchad. Au total, 48 025 ménages réfugiés à Aboutengué, Metché, Zabout, Djabal, Goz-Amir et Kerfi ont reçu les résultats de leur évaluation. Ces résultats permettront au HCR et à ses partenaires de mieux cibler et prioriser l’assistance en fonction des vulnérabilités et capacités identifiées, tout en renforçant le suivi des ménages ayant des besoins spécifiques. La communication des résultats et le mécanisme de gestion des réclamations se sont poursuivis à Metché, Milé et Touloum, tandis que les préparatifs ont été finalisés à Amdjarass en vue du déploiement de l’ABVC à Ouré Cassoni à partir du 3 novembre. Entre le 2 et le 8 novembre, le HCR et ses partenaires ont facilité le départ de 21 réfugiés soudanais de l’est du Tchad vers le Canada. Douze réfugiés ont bénéficié d’un programme de la réinstallation, deux d’une reunification familiale et sept personnes reinstallés au Canada par les voies complémentaires. Le HCR poursuit ses efforts en faveur des solutions durables dans l’est du Tchad, notamment à travers l’accompagnement des réfugiés et le traitement des dossiers de réinstallation et de regroupement familial.

items.title: History of UNHCR in Türkiye 1960 to 2026
items.blurb:
Country: Türkiye
Source: UN High Commissioner for Refugees

Please refer to the attached file.

UNHCR has been present in Türkiye for more than six decades. Its presence was formally endorsed in 1960, marking the beginning of a long-standing partnership with the Government and people of Türkiye. In April 1962, Türkiye ratified the 1951 Convention relating to the Status of Refugees, becoming its 34th State party. Türkiye subsequently ratified the 1967 Protocol Relating to the Status of Refugees in 1968. In June 1967, UN High Commissioner for Refugees Prince Sadruddin Aga Khan made an official visit to Türkiye. He was received by President Cevdet Sunay and Prime Minister Süleyman Demirel. During his visit, the High Commissioner opened a refugee housing project in Istanbul, largely financed by UNHCR. At that time, UNHCR reportedly supported several projects that helped 1,400 refugees in Türkiye. Over the decades, UNHCR and Türkiye have responded to a series of humanitarian crises as refugees and asylum-seekers arrived from Iran in 1979, Iraq in 1988, Bosnia in 1993, Kosovo* in 1999, and finally Syria in 2011. Each crisis prompted significant scale-up of UNHCR’s operations. Until the early 1980s, UNHCR’s work in Türkiye largely focused on refugees from Eastern Europe. That changed between August 1982 and November 1984, when the Turkish Government, with support of the Red Crescent and UNHCR resettled around 4,000 Afghan refugees of Turkic origin from Pakistan to Türkiye. They were Kirghiz, Kazakh, Uzbek, Turkman and Uighur families, who had found temporary asylum in Pakistan, before being resettled to the east and south-east of Türkiye. In 1985, UNHCR started conducting its mandated Refugee Status Determination (RSD) in Türkiye. During the 1991 Gulf War, Türkiye faced one of the largest and fastest refugee movements. Around 500,000 Iraqis gathered in mountainous areas along the border. UNHCR provided tents in the Habur Hajj camp in Silopi. UN High Commissioner for Refugees Madam Sadako Ogata visited Türkiye to support the humanitarian response. In 2011, as thousands of refugees and asylum seekers arrived from Syria, Türkiye introduced temporary protection for all Syrians seeking safety in the country. UNHCR was invited to contribute to the development of Türkiye's new asylum legislation. To support the most vulnerable refugees, UNHCR provided tents, blankets and bed mats through the Turkish Red Crescent Society. Initially intended for newly arrived Syrians in Hatay, these supplies were also distributed to communities affected by the earthquake in Van. In 2011 alone, UNHCR provided 4,000 tents, 50,000 blankets and 10,000 bed mats.

items.title: UNICEF fast facts: World leaders meet in Manila to end violence against children
items.blurb:
Country: World
Source: UN Children's Fund

MANILA/NEW YORK, 18 November 2026 – As government ministers, partners, survivors, and young people gather in Manila, Philippines, for the Second Global Ministerial Conference on Ending Violence Against Children this week (18 – 19th November), UNICEF is calling on governments to turn commitments made in Bogotá two years ago into sustained investment in the solutions proven to keep children safe.

“Violence against children is not inevitable. We know what works to prevent it, and we have seen what is possible when governments invest in protecting children,” said UNICEF Deputy Executive Director Ted Chaiban. “But commitments alone will not keep children safe. We need sustained investment in strong child protection systems, support for parents and caregivers, and safe schools and communities. The true measure of our progress will be whether every child can grow up free from violence, wherever they live.”

According to the latest available global data:

  • 1.6 billion children (2 in 3) experience violent discipline (physical punishment, psychological aggression, or both) by parents or other caregivers at home, including 1 in 8 who experience severe physical punishment.

  • Around 650 million girls and women (1 in 5) and around 410 – 530 million boys and men (around 1 in 7) alive today experienced sexual violence as children. This includes more than 370 million girls and women (1 in 8) and between 240 and 310 million boys and men (around 1 in 11) who experienced rape or sexual assault.

  • In fragile settings, the risk for girls is even greater, with slightly more than 1 in 4 experiencing rape or sexual assault in childhood.

  • Around 610 million children (1 in 4) live with mothers who experienced intimate partner violence in the past year.

  • In a single year, around 20 million children aged 12 to 17 (almost 1 in 5) across 21 countries experienced technology-facilitated sexual exploitation and abuse.

    • Nearly 60 per cent of these cases took place on social media platforms.
    • More than half (57 per cent) involved someone the child already knew: a peer, partner, friend or family member.
    • More than 40 per cent of cases were never shared with anyone, and fewer than 1 per cent were reported to the police, social workers or helplines. The most common reason for not reporting the incident was not knowing where to go or who to tell.

  • Every 4 minutes, somewhere in the world, a child is killed by an act of violence.

UNICEF works with governments around the world to protect children from violence before it starts and to support them when it happens. Since 2022, UNICEF has reached 60.2 million parents and caregivers with support to raise their children without violence and helped 19.9 million children who experienced violence across 112 countries to get the care and protection they needed. Legal bans on violent discipline that UNICEF has supported now protect more than 40 million children.

UNICEF is calling on governments to fully finance and scale up proven solutions to end violence against children, including supporting parents and caregivers to provide safe and nurturing care; creating safe and enabling schools where children can learn and thrive, and strengthening accessible, inclusive, and resilient response services for every child experiencing violence.

UNICEF, the United Nations agency for children, works to protect the rights of every child, everywhere, especially the most disadvantaged children and in the toughest places to reach. Across more than 190 countries and territories, we do whatever it takes to help children survive, thrive, and fulfil their potential.
